Job description 
The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays an important role in determining how tumors respond to radiotherapy. Features such as stromal composition, hypoxia, and cellular senescence can contribute to radioresistance and may therefore represent potential therapeutic targets.
In this PhD project, you will investigate how modulation of the TME can enhance the response to radiotherapy. The project will combine patient-derived models and in vivo tumor models to study how different TME characteristics contribute to treatment response and to explore potential strategies to target these mechanisms. A range of complementary preclinical approaches is used, including hypoxia modulation, targeting of senescent cells or cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs), (image-guided) radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibition. Treatment response and underlying mechanisms will be assessed through readouts such as DNA damage and repair, tumor growth and characterization of the TME. The precise experimental approaches will be guided by the scientific findings and direction of the project.

REQUIREMENTS:
Profile 
 Requirements 
 An MSc degree in Biomedical Sciences, Biology, Cancer Biology, or a related field, or an equivalent degree,
 A strong interest in preclinical cancer research,
 Motivated to investigate biological mechanisms underlying treatment response,
 Curious, enthusiastic about experimental science, and enjoy working in an interdisciplinary research environment.
Experience with molecular and cellular biology, tumor biology, radiobiology or immunology is an advantage. Experience with preclinical animal models is welcome, and candidates holding an Article 9 certificate for working with experimental animals are especially encouraged to apply.

CONTRACT: 4 years

academictransfer:363769.description:
The Department of Mathematics of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam welcomes applications for a fully-funded, 4-year PhD position in causal inference.
You will join the “Safe Causal Inference” consortium. Causal inference studies what assumptions are needed, and which methods you can use when those assumptions are met, to reliably conclude that “A causes B” and not just “A is correlated with B”. The consortium aims to incorporate all uncertainties into causal inferences, combining information obtained under alternative assumptions. In a team of 8 PhD researchers and 5 Principal Investigators located throughout the Netherlands, you’ll join us in developing a novel, iterative approach to causal inference that combines the strengths of subject-matter knowledge and the flexibility of data-driven algorithms.
You will work on the subproject “Triangulation of performance assessment methods for conditional causal quantities”. This PhD project investigates how to reliably assess the performance of estimators of conditional causal effects (such as CATE estimators and predictions under interventions). The core problem is that evaluating an estimator requires counterfactual outcomes in the evaluation dataset, but deriving those outcomes itself relies on causal assumptions, meaning the evaluation can be just as assumption-dependent as the estimator it's meant to assess.
You will examine whether combining evaluation results across different datasets, different causal assumptions, and different evaluation approaches (counterfactual, factual, and benchmarking against trials) leads to a more complete and reliable picture of a causal relationship. The goal is to develop a framework that helps data analysts choose the best evaluation strategy depending on which assumptions they are willing to make.
You will be jointly supervised by dr. Stéphanie van der Pas (VU), dr. Nan van Geloven (LUMC) and dr. Jeremy Labrecque (ErasmusMC). Your main working location will be the Mathematics department at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, where you will join dr. Stéphanie van der Pas’ research group on causal inference.
We are an inclusive, interdisciplinary group, and diversity and internationalism is at the heart of our research principles, as well as our teaching practice.
The preferred starting date is: as soon as possible, ideally before 01.02.2027.
Applications from all groups currently under-represented in academic posts are especially encouraged. We particularly welcome applications from women and people with an ethnic minority background.
 Your duties 
 doing research towards writing a PhD thesis
 teaching tasks (roughly 15% of your time), for instance supervising exercise classes

REQUIREMENTS:
a (prospective) MSc. degree in Mathematics, Statistics or Econometrics (or an equivalent thereof)
 good communication skills in English
Priority will be given to candidates with:
 a strong background in statistics
 experience with causal inference
 affinity with programming in R or python

CONTRACT: 1 year

Are you eager to dive into cutting-edge neuromodulation and real-world symptom monitoring? 
As a research assistant in our team, you will be running TMS sessions, working with intensive longitudinal data from daily life, and contributing to a new, state-informed approach to brain stimulation. This position offers the unique opportunity to work at the intersection of neuroscience, data science, and clinical research, with room for creativity, technical exploration, and meaningful impact. Here you'll have the chance to help deliver an iTBS protocol targeting the left prefrontal cortex, to model how cognitive fatigue fluctuates from moment to moment, and to explore who responds to stimulation and when. Curious minds are very welcome.
 Context  
In this project, members of the Cognitive Neuropsychology Department at Tilburg University aim to bridge real-time symptom monitoring in daily life with a pilot neuromodulation design, to better understand when and for whom stimulation may be most effective. By identifying dynamic fatigue profiles in students with elevated fatigue and relating them to short-term response to iTBS, the project lays the groundwork for more personalized, state-informed brain stimulation in clinical populations experiencing "mental fog".
 Your position  
As a Research Assistant, you will support an ongoing pilot project that combines ecological momentary assessment (EMA) with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), with the broader goal of understanding cognitive fatigue as a dynamic process. Your work will involve a short literature study, hands-on involvement in data collection (EMA via a smartphone app and iTBS sessions in the lab), and initial support of the data analysis. Over time, you'll help document the workflows that link daily-life symptom dynamics to short-term response to stimulation.
 You'll mainly focus on the data-collection (recruitment, running TMS sessions, monitoring EMA compliance) and later on explore preliminary analyses (processing intensive longitudinal data).
 You'll be actively involved in:
 Recruiting and scheduling participants and running EMA and iTBS sessions
 Following predefined TMS procedures (resting motor threshold, Beam F3 localization, delivering the iTBS protocol) under supervision
 Monitoring and managing the EMA data collection and participant compliance
 Contributing to the processing and analysis of intensive longitudinal (EMA) and stimulation data
 Summarizing results and documenting workflows, and collaborating with the research team on interim findings and next steps
 This way, you'll have an influence on the direction of the project and the opportunity to apply and further refine valuable skills at the intersection of neuromodulation, data science, and clinical research.
 What your typical week might look like: 
You'll split your time between the lab and independent work, i.e. running participant sessions (TMS and EMA onboarding), meeting with supervisors to discuss progress and troubleshoot technical or practical challenges, and documenting your workflow and results. Some weeks may be focused on data collection and participant contact, others on managing and interpreting the EMA and stimulation data, or preparing summary reports.

REQUIREMENTS:
Your profile 
You are a motivated recent graduate, with a strong analytical mindset and an interest in neuromodulation, symptom dynamics, and technological innovation in clinical care.
 We are looking for someone who meets the following criteria:
 You recently completed a bachelor’s or master's degree in (neuro-)psychology, social or biomedical sciences, (bio-)engineering, or a related field.
 You have demonstrable affinity with neuroscience and/or human research (e.g. through coursework, your thesis, internship, or previous research projects).
 You are comfortable working with statistical data analysis software or very motivated to learn new tools (e.g. R, STATA, or alternative coding).
 Scientific and/or practical experience with neuroscientific methods such as neuromodulation (TMS) and/or intensive longitudinal/EMA data is not required but is an asset.
 You are eager to take initiative, enjoy solving methodological and practical challenges.
 You collaborate well but can also work independently when running sessions or exploring analyses.
 You are reliable and comfortable in participant-facing tasks, and you handle sensitive data with care.
 You have sufficient proficiency in English to read scientific literature, communicate in a research context, and document your work clearly; proficiency in Dutch is an asset for participant contact.
 Competencies:
 Organizing ability: you can coordinate and keep track of a multimodal data collection (participant scheduling, TMS sessions, and continuous EMA sampling running in parallel), managing the practical logistics.
 Initiative: you take ownership of tasks, identify opportunities for improvement, and follow through independently.
 Accuracy: you pay attention to detail and ensure the quality and traceability of your work.
 Collaboration: you can communicate effectively within a research team and contribute constructively to shared goals.

Are you a systems thinker passionate about bending the curve of biodiversity loss in agricultural landscapes? Are you looking for a meaningful research path with impact on the ground? Are you eager to join a stimulating environment, collaborate across academic fields, and engage with private and public actors? Are you enthusiastic to dive into effective planning and governance arrangements for biodiversity recovery in agricultural landscapes? Do you speak English and Dutch? Then, this PhD position might be the perfect fit for you. 
Biodiversity recovery is essential to sustain resilient food systems, robust businesses, and healthy societies. A transition to a nature-inclusive dairy sector in the Netherlands is pivotal to biodiversity recovery, because of its influence in shaping landscapes through land use and management, and because of its socio-economic relevance. DECISION is a transdisciplinary project involving farmers, dairy companies, financial and service sectors, and local communities, to co-create and accelerate the transition to a resilient and nature-inclusive future. DECISION will count on a broad group of experts, four fully funded PhDs candidates and one postdoc.
For this position, we are looking for a PhD candidate eager to deal with the complexity of public and private governance efforts coming together in landscapes and at farm level, and the need to design coordinated action. In that role, you will build on and integrate the work of your fellow PhD candidates, co-develop a theory of change integrating coordinated public and private action and monitoring, explore synergies and tensions in multi-actor governance and planning, and help bridge research and education.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Develop a Research Proposal and a Training and Supervision Plan, to structure the 5-year project with a 0.8fte PhD trajectory
 Advancing conceptual thinking by linking and comparing business-to-business approaches with collective action and landscape governance
 Conducting and analyzing semi-structured interviews and workshops with stakeholders
 Implement a Theory of Change approach and other approaches for knowledge co-production with stakeholders
 Disseminate results by publishing papers in scientific journals, presenting in international conferences, and creating content items dedicated to stakeholders and students

This PhD position will be situated between the Land Use Planning Group of Wageningen University & Research and the Animal Production Systems (APS) group . You will be supervised by Dr Judith Westerink (LUP) and Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch (APS). The work of Dr Judith Westerink focuses on transformative landscape governance, in particular related to biodiversity and dairy farming systems. The work of Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch focuses on understanding the complex interactions between livestock, nature (biodiversity and ecosystem services) and economy, to design enabling environments for the transitions to nature-inclusive agroecosystems.

Are you interested in the spatial and socio-cultural interactions between the rural and the urban, how these relate to representations and senses of rural and urban places, and how life course and generational differences may influence this? And would you like to conduct research in an interdisciplinary consortium of Dutch universities, universities of applied sciences and societal partners? Then this postdoc position is perfect for you.
 What are you going to do? 
 The Faculty of Spatial Sciences of the University of Groningen is looking to appoint a postdoctoral researcher “ Socio-Cultural Aspects of Rural-Urban Interactions” . The position is embedded in the NWO KIC research project Fertile Soils for future generations: integrated spatial strategies and effective governance for coherent rural-urban regions. Fertile soils addresses different aspects of rural-urban relations, related to the landscape services they provide. Landscape services are ecosystem services that are offered and consumed within one landscape, such as food production, recreation, biodiversity, flood protection, water retention, space for living, space for economic activities, social cohesion and regional identity. The project consists of 7 work packages. The postdoc Socio-Cultural Aspects of Rural-Urban Interactions is embedded in WP4. WP4 aims to investigate how interactions between rural and urban are experienced in people's daily lives, how they envision these interactions to be in the future, and how this can contribute to a sense of connectedness to the place and/or a regional identity.
 At the Faculty of Spatial Sciences (FSS) the research team includes Tialda Haartsen (professor rural geography, WP4 lead), Charlotte Oosterhuis (PhD, WP4), Jesse Lindenhovius (PhD, WP3), Koen Salemink (supervisor, WP4), Martijn van der Heide and Gunnar Mallon (supervisors, WP3). WP4 also consist of Kristin Zlatanova-Panova (PhD), Jasper de Vries and Marlies Meijer (supervisors) from Wageningen University. FSS is also region-coordinator of the Fertile Soils region Hogeland – city of Groningen. As postdoc, you will perform some of the WP4 research tasks, in close collaboration with the other team members and with the consortium partners in the project.
 These tasks include:
 Investigate rural-urban interactions and socio-cultural meanings of urban and rural areas.
 Explore current and future needs in rural-urban interactions (e.g. regional identity and sense of place) from an intergenerational and life course perspective through representative survey, interviews, and focus group discussions with young societally active groups.
 Relate and integrate the WP4 findings to the other WPs.
 Write academic and popular publications about these research activities.
 PhD supervision.
 Be the contact person for the region Hogeland-Groningen.
 Perform some occasional teaching duties in one of the participating faculties.

REQUIREMENTS:
Our ideal candidate has:
 A PhD degree in a field of study relevant to the topic of the project (e.g. human geography, rural studies or sociology). Completed or to be completed in the near future.
 Strong conceptual thinking skills and a proactive and a proactive and independent work attitude.
 Experience with quantitative and qualitative research methods.
 Publications in international peer-reviewed academic journals that testify of your interest in aspects of rural-urban relations.
 The skills to present academic analyses to varied audiences including scientific professionals and policy makers. Also, you are comfortable building and maintaining a professional network to regional and national policy makers that are affiliated or relevant to the research that you are performing.
  A fluency in English (reading, writing, speaking).
 A fluency in Dutch, as some of the data gathering will take place in this language.

Shape the future of cancer therapy through nanomedicine process engineering. 
 Join as a PhD candidate to design lipid nanoparticles using computational modeling with real-world validation. 
 Job description 
SPARC (Scalable Personalized Nanotherapeutics for Cancer Treatment) is an ambitious research program dedicated to making advanced cancer therapies more effective and accessible, particularly for patients with hard-to-treat “cold tumors.” By developing personalized nanomedicines, SPARC aims to improve patient survival through innovations such as tumor-on-a-chip platforms that reduce reliance on animal testing, and novel manufacturing technologies that enhance therapeutic efficacy and product stability.
As part of this program, we are seeking a highly motivated Ph.D. student with an interest in cross-disciplinary research to join a shared position between the Precision Therapeutics group (Dr. Alina Rwei) in the Chemical Engineering department and the Complex Fluid Processing group (Prof. Johan Padding) in the Process & Energy department of TU Delft. The position will formally be at Precision Therapeutics.
The project is embedded in a strong academic–industrial network and offers close collaboration with leading pharmaceutical partners, including Merck KGaA and Johnson & Johnson.
This project focuses on purification of the output stream of lipid-based drug delivery nanoparticles manufacturing systems. These streams typically contain solvent, lipids and unencapsulated drug components, which need to be removed by dilution and subsequent ultra- or diafiltration. Current purification systems, typically based on (alternating) tangential flow filtration, suffer from loss of expensive lipid nanoparticles and membrane fouling, necessitating expensive regular replacement of the membranes.
Your task will be to engineer innovative purification systems, e.g. by changing membrane materials and designing novel filtration flow geometries, that minimize loss of lipid nanoparticles and maximise throughput. In the design you will explore modularization options for relatively quick and low-cost replacement of filtration system components. The project also involves close interaction with other research teams within the SPARC consortium, e.g., molecular mechanisms for membrane fouling are investigated.
Key Responsibilities
 Computational modelling with CFD simulations: 
 Investigate the flow, diffusion and filtration in tangential flow filtration systems
 Implement correlations to model build-up of fouling and its effects on filtration capacity
 Develop novel flow geometries that balance: 
 Throughput (maximising production rates)
 Mechanical stress on lipid nanoparticles (minimising loss of LNPs)
 Experimental verification
 Experimentally verify the use of alternative membranes for LNP purification.
 Experimentally verify modularisation options for the purification train, including use of quick connectors. 
 Job requirements 
 MSc or equivalent in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Nanotechnology or related field
 Analytical mindset with ability to work across computational and experimental domains

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional.

We are looking for a PostDoc who will do research on the intersection of machine learning (ML) and statistics. More specifically, the focus is on the development of algorithmic improvements in causal inference and reinforcement learning through the cross fertilization of machine learning and statistical approaches and applying these innovations in a health setting.
The position is embedded in two projects which act as application domains. First of all, the ten-year gravitation grant Stress in Action, funded through NWO (Dutch National Science Foundation). The goal of the project is to move stress research from the lab into daily life, and hence, the use cases of the methodological innovations will focus on applications to stress-related data, such as wearables, ecological momentary assessments, and other types of questionnaires. Secondly, the ZonMW funded MINMED project which aims to unlock causal effects of interventions in elderly care from observational data.
A variety of academic partners are involved in the two projects, including Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Amsterdam UMC, Erasmus MC, University of Twente, University of Groningen, UMC Groningen, and Utrecht University.
The position is embedded in the Quantitative Data Analytics (QDA) group of the VU in close collaboration with the Amsterdam UMC, Erasmus MC and the University of Groningen. The QDA group focuses on both fundamental and application-driven research in ML.
We are looking for candidates with experience in the area of machine learning or statistics, with a special preference for those with expertise in causal inference and/or reinforcement learning, ideally complemented with a solid background in statistics. We are interested in attracting a PostDoc who is able to perform ground-breaking research on fundamental aspects of machine learning and statistics and wants to apply these innovations in the context of the Stress in Action and MINMED projects.
 Your duties 
The PostDoc position is focused on performing research and contains the following duties:
 performing research in the field of machine learning and publishing in top AI and ML conferences
 participating in the QDA group of VU (lead by Mark Hoogendoorn), the Biostatistics group of Erasmus MC (led by Dimitris Rizopoulos), and Laura Bringmann's intensive longitudinal data lab at the University of Groningen.
 contributing to the Stress in Action and MINMED projects and interacting with the different partners and stakeholders in the project
 contributing to some teaching activities and possibly supervising Bachelor and Master students (20% of the time)

REQUIREMENTS:
We will base our selection on the following components:
 a PhD degree in an area relevant to machine learning and/or statistics
 prior experience in machine learning, ideally also on applications in the health domain, demonstrated by relevant publications
 a strong record of computer programming, with experience in pytorch and/or tensorflow
 demonstrated ability to work both independently and as a team member
As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. We believe that diversity in all its complexity is invaluable for the quality of our teaching, research and service. We are always looking for talent with diverse backgrounds and experiences. This also means that we are committed to creating an inclusive community so that we can use diversity as an asset.
We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. Therefore we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements.

Wil je studenten, promovendi en onderzoekers helpen om wetenschappelijke informatie doelgericht, zorgvuldig en reproduceerbaar te vinden?
Als informatiespecialist educatie bij de Universiteitsbibliotheek Utrecht geef je onderwijs op het gebied van informatievaardigheden en systematisch zoeken. Daarnaast geef je richting aan de manier waarop we omgaan met AI in het zoeken, beoordelen en gebruiken van wetenschappelijke informatie én aan de vertaling daarvan naar ons onderwijs.
 Wat ga je doen? 
Als informatiespecialist adviseer en ondersteun je onderzoekers en studenten binnen Medische Wetenschappen, het UMC Utrecht, Diergeneeskunde en Bètawetenschappen. Met jouw werk draag je direct bij aan de kwaliteit van wetenschappelijk onderzoek en help je studenten om efficiënter en zorgvuldiger met informatie om te gaan. Je doet dit samen met één vaste collega-informatiespecialist: jouw zwaartepunt ligt bij Diergeneeskunde en Bèta, maar het lesgeven, het ontwikkelen van nieuw onderwijs en de intake van aanvragen pakken jullie samen op.
Je verzorgt trainingen in informatievaardigheden voor bachelor- en masterstudenten en trainingen in systematisch zoeken voor promovendi, zowel in groepen als één-op-één. Je ontwikkelt daarvoor nieuw onderwijs en houdt de bestaande leermaterialen actueel, zoals LibGuides, modules en presentaties. Je weet hoe je gericht en systematisch zoekt in de bibliotheekcollectie en in openbare bronnen en bent daarvoor binnen het team het aanspreekpunt. Die kennis breng je op een duidelijke en enthousiasmerende manier over, afgestemd op je publiek: een eerstejaars bachelor vraagt om een ander verhaal dan een promovendus.
Daarnaast begeleid je zoekconsulten en ondersteun je systematic review-projecten: van het scherp krijgen van de vraag tot de zoekstrategie, de documentatie en de peer review van de search. Je legt je werk zo vast dat een ander de zoekactie later kan reproduceren. Ook onderhoud je contact met de facultaire onderwijscoördinatoren, zodat ons aanbod blijft aansluiten op het curriculum, en verbeter je dat aanbod op basis van evaluaties. Het thema AI en systematisch zoeken trek jij. Je test tools zelf uit, vertaalt wat werkt naar onze dienstverlening en draagt bij aan de AI-visie van de afdeling ter ondersteuning van de faculteiten in lijn met onze systematic reviewprojecten.
Je werkt binnen de afdeling Onderwijsondersteuning van de Universiteitsbibliotheek Utrecht. Deze afdeling ontwikkelt en verzorgt onderwijs op het gebied van informatievaardigheden voor alle faculteiten en ondersteunt daarnaast op het gebied van auteursrecht en open leermaterialen. Binnen de afdeling is veel ruimte voor kennisdeling, samenwerking en innovatie. We werken continu aan het verbeteren van ons onderwijsaanbod en spelen in op ontwikkelingen binnen het vakgebied en het onderwijs.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je hebt een academische opleiding.
 Je hebt ruime, aantoonbare ervaring met systematisch zoeken in een academische context: je vertaalt een vage vraag naar concepten, synoniemen en een getoetste zoekstring, en documenteert die zo dat een ander hem een jaar later kan herhalen.
 Je hebt ervaring met het geven van trainingen of andere vormen van het overbrengen van kennis, stemt je verhaal af op het niveau van je publiek en coacht liever dan dat je overneemt: een promovendus vertrekt bij jou met een eigen zoekstrategie.
 Je kunt je goed verplaatsen in het perspectief van de onderzoeker: je hoort ook wat iemand niet zegt en vraagt door totdat de werkelijke informatiebehoefte helder is.
 Je deelt materialen en zoekstrategieën met collega's en maakt je een nieuwe database of tool snel genoeg eigen om die binnen een blok in je onderwijs te gebruiken.
 Je beheerst het Nederlands uitstekend (C1) en het Engels goed (B2).
Verder is het gewenst als je:
 Een achtergrond hebt in de life sciences of ervaring hebt met onderzoek in dat domein;
 Bekend bent met het opzetten en uitvoeren van systematisch reviews en met peer review van zoekstrategieën (bijvoorbeeld PRESS);
 Al met AI-tools voor zoeken hebt gewerkt en daar een onderbouwd oordeel over hebt;
 Ervaring hebt met het ontwikkelen van leermaterialen.

Are you fascinated by the intersection of Physics, Chemistry and materials science? Do you want to contribute to protecting monuments including World Heritage Sites from degradation caused by rising damp?
 The Institute of Physics at the University is seeking an ambitious PhD candidate to investigate the effectiveness of damp-proofing products across multiple length scales.
 Join Us! 
Rising damp from groundwater represents a critical threat to buildings worldwide. Some building-preservation treatments (most of the times polymers) are used to reduce rising damp , that is the moisture uptake from the ground moving upward through porous brick, stone, or mortar by capillary action. These treatments are supposed to create a water-repellent zone in order to interrupt upward moisture transport.
However, the fundamental mechanisms governing the spreading and polycondensation at the microscale, and thus the effectiveness, of such treatments in porous building materials remain largely unexplored. Critical knowledge gaps exist regarding the multiscale behaviour of these treatments, from microscale pore interactions to macroscale building performance.
This project will advance beyond the state of the art by elucidating for the first time the dynamics of spreading and polycondensation of chemical damp proofing products by real-time visualization of these processes at the pore scale. You will use novel experimental methods developed in our laboratory by combining fluorescent viscosity-sensitive probes and confocal/infrared microscopy with mechanical measurements to correlate the microscale of pore interaction to the macroscale behaviour.
Together with a diverse stakeholders group, including chemical product manufacturers, governmental conservation agencies, building asset owners, and contractors, and in collaboration with TU Delft (the Architecture Department) we will establish the knowledge and tools to improve the effectiveness of chemical damp proofing interventions and significantly reduce the estimated €19 million annual costs of chemical treatments in the Netherlands.
Your research will be part of the Soft Matter cluster at the Van der Waals-Zeeman Institute for Experimental Physics (IoP-WZI) at the University of Amsterdam, under the supervision of Prof. Noushine Shahidzadeh (expert on crystallization and sol-gel process in confinement) and Prof. Hannelore Derluyn (expert in micro-CT 3D imaging for porous media).
 This is what you will do 
You will conduct pioneering research combining advanced imaging techniques with experimental characterization to elucidate the effects of different variables on the effectiveness of chemical damp proofing products, with the final goal of increasing the success of such barrier treatments against rising damp in (historic) masonry.
You will Study
 the Rheological changes of the product during polycondensation
 Reaction and aging in quasi-2D micromodels of porous media designed in the lab. Results will bring valuable pore-scale information on gelation and polycondensation, not accessible by other advanced imaging techniques such as NMR and X-ray Computed Tomography (XCT).
 The dynamics of spreading of chemical products at different conditions in different porous materials using fluorescent viscosity-sensitive probes and confocal/infrared microscopy, and also by XCT scans, to get valuable information on the final deposition, following polycondensation at the microscale, and the results on the macroscale behaviour.
 Your core responsibilities include: 
 Conducting independent experimental research at different scales from bulk to confinement under various climatic conditions,
 Performing systematic studies in microfluidic channels and real porous building materials (limestone and sandstone) at the laboratory scale under controlled environmental cycling.
 Using advanced imaging and characterization techniques including optical and electron microscopy, IR and Raman spectroscopy, MRI, and X-ray microtomography to track polycondensation in real time.
 Publishing your findings in peer-reviewed international journals and presenting at international conferences
 Contributing to teaching activities by assisting in undergraduate and master's courses in physics.
 Collaborating with other members of Prof. Shahidzadeh and Prof. Hannelore Derluyn's group and making the link with our collaborator at TUDelft.
 What we ask of you 
 Your experience and profile: 
 A completed Master's degree in Physics, Materials Science, Physical Chemistry, Chemistry, or a closely related field.
 Strong interest in experimental research combining materials science, sol-gel process, and applications to real-world problems.
 Affinity with experimental techniques including microscopy, spectroscopy, and/or imaging methods.
 Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment.

How to best incorporate New Genomic Techniques to solve challenging issues in plant breeding? The recent approval by the European Parliament of new legislation to allow application of gene editing approaches in plant breeding, offers new opportunities to address this. One such challenge is to improve complex traits such as crop tolerance to dynamic environmental conditions in the current era of global climate change and how to best incorporate this in plant breeding strategies.
Anticipating the new legislation, the INPROBED project has been granted, which aims to precisely identify and modify cis -regulatory elements and transcription factor genes that control key physiological pathways to specifically adjust targeted gene expression to reshape complex traits.
The project will develop a breakthrough science-enabled technology platform to improve tomato heat, drought and nutrient deficiency tolerance and the nutritional status of tomato fruits for human health. In this project, you will investigate the tomato response to Zn and Fe deficiency and design strategies to improve the Zn/Fe nutritional status of tomatoes for human health.
You will generate dedicated (single-cell) transcriptional data sets feeding into the MNase-defined cistrome occupancy (MOA-seq) analysis of transcription factor binding of tomato promoter elements controlling the Zn and Fe deficiency responsive gene expression. You will design specific constructs to edit transcription factor genes and their target promoters, and analyse the effects of optimized gene expression regulation on plant performance under optimal and field-like conditions at the Netherlands Plant Eco-phenotyping Centre. Your research aims to improve tomato Zn and Fe uptake under regular field conditions and to enhance the Zn and Fe nutritional status of tomato fruits.
INPROBED is part of the prestigious European Innovation Council (EIC) Pathfinder Challenge programme addressing innovative biotechnology for climate resilient crops. It brings together excellent expertise from world-leading European research institutions and companies. You will work closely together with researchers across the consortium to predict and edit targeted gene promoters, to design relevant constructs for gene editing and to evaluate the gene-edited plants to establish this topic firmly into the plant breeding domain.
Within Wageningen University, you will be embedded in the Laboratory of Genetics of the Plant Sciences Group, and collaborate with researchers and thesis students investigating the genetic basis of plant adaptation to the environment, focusing on plant nutrition, metal tolerance and photosynthesis. Your research is expected to deliver fundamental insights into the genetic regulation of tomato gene expression and provide strong experimental validation of the technology platform to improve complex crop traits through gene editing of gene expression regulators.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 To design the experimental setup for gene expression analysis of tomato response to Zn and Fe deficiency, and of Zn and Fe loading into the developing fruit.
 The biological interpretation of MOA-seq analysis with respect to the tomato response to Zn and Fe deficiency.
 The experimental validation of gene-edited tomato plants with respect to plant growth and development and their ionome under optimal, natural and mineral-stress conditions.
 To establish a fruitful collaboration with international partners in the project and to supervise a part-time technician on the project.
 To write manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals reporting on the results of your research.
 Your team 
You will work with international partners in the project and with other members in the Botanical Genetics team of the Laboratory of Genetics of Wageningen University, which is led by Prof. Mark Aarts You will work in close collaboration with a technician to be appointed on the project.
 You will work here 
Wageningen UR has a global reputation for its ground-breaking research and innovative education in the fields of food and health, sustainable agrosystems, the rural environment, and societal development - all of which make an essential contribution to the quality of life, i.e. the supply of safe and healthy food and drink, on the one hand, and the chance to live, work and play in a balanced ecosystem with a large variety of plants and animals on the other. Within Wageningen UR, the Plant Sciences Group brings together science education and scientific, strategic and applied research in the fields of biology, of plants in relation to their environment, of plant-related organisms and of plant production. The Laboratory of Genetics is interested in heredity in general, in particular the origin, architecture and consequences of genetic variation of a wide range of organisms across the biological kingdoms.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are an ambitious, curiosity-driven and collaboration-oriented plant scientist, with:
 a strong academic track record and a PhD in plant biotechnology, plant molecular genetics or a related topic;
 experience with plant mineral homeostasis and/or tomato research;
 demonstrated expertise in the analysis of large data-sets;
 a strong interest in experimental research;
 an excellent oral and written English communication skills.
In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level C1 .

academictransfer:363916.description:
PhD position on local food web dynamics within offshore wind farms in the North Sea POWER (Progress in Offshore Wind Ecological Research) consortium. 
As offshore wind farms rapidly expand in the North Sea, mitigating their ecological impact on marine ecosystems is critical. The North Sea POWER project addresses this challenge by filling vital knowledge gaps regarding underwater noise, biomass and water flows, and wildlife disturbance (such as seabirds and bats) to support a sustainable green energy transition. By reducing uncertainty in models and identifying effective mitigation options, North Sea POWER supports offshore wind development that protects marine ecosystems while contributing to a sustainable energy future.
The project is funded through the Dutch Research Agenda (NWA), developed in collaboration with the Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy.
Led by Wageningen University & Research, the project brings together a transdisciplinary consortium of leading academic institutions, societal stakeholders, conservation organisations, and energy sector partners. More about the consortium .
This position is one of twelve PhD and postdoc positions across the consortium. You will be part of a team working on shared questions, with joint meetings, fieldwork and training alongside your own project. You will be hosted at Wageningen Marine Research in Den Helder, where you will study how fouling communities in offshore wind farms affect local food web dynamics and carbon cycling in close collaboration with Wageningen University. Part of the molecular lab work will be performed in the lab of Marine Animal Ecology in Wageningen.
 Are you interested in how biofouling communities in offshore wind farms affect local food web dynamics and carbon cycling? 
We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to join our research team on biofouling with a focus on quantifying how biofouling communities influence primary and secondary production and blue carbon sequestration in the seabed. By combining laboratory experiments, in-situ fieldwork observations, and ecosystem modelling, your work will help refine current ecosystem-scale models and inform environmental impact assessments.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 conduct laboratory experiments to measure and quantify grazing rates, carbon biomass, prey preferences, particle export, and faeces sinking velocity rates across different fouling species;
 execute field surveys from research vessels;
 integrate empirical data into conceptual models;
 publish research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present them at national and international conferences;
 mentor BSc/MSc students.
 Your team 
You will be part of Wageningen Marine Research (WMR – Den Helder), as a member of the Theme Team North Sea Reefs with Dr. Joop Coolen , and Dr. Ninon Mavraki as your daily supervisors, and you are also part of the Marine Animal Ecology Group (MAE) supervised by the Associate Professor Reindert Nijland at Wageningen University and Research. In Den Helder a broad group of scientists, analysts, field workers and students work on a variety of topics, such as benthic ecology, seals, seabirds, bats and other species. You will be a member of the theme team North Sea Reefs, with multiple colleagues specialising in the ecology of natural and artificial reefs in the North Sea. Furthermore, you will have the opportunity to design experiments involving molecular tools, such as eDNA and DNA metabarcoding, which then will be performed at the molecular laboratory of MAE in Wageningen University.
 You will work here 
The position is available within Wageningen University & Research at the Marine Animal Ecology group. The organisation has good and flexible employment conditions, including good education and training facilities for PhD students. Your working location will be at Wageningen Marine Research in Den Helder, the Netherlands, where the daily supervisors Joop Coolen and Ninon Mavraki are located. WMR is an applied research institute with 3 locations (Den Helder, IJmuiden and Yerseke) in the Netherlands. Research areas in Den Helder include coastal and offshore North Sea, tropics and (ant)arctic regions. In addition to ecological research, WMR advises the government regarding protection of species and habitats, pollution, and other anthropogenic interactions with ecology, and collaborate with industry, i.a. to study nature inclusive designs. Facilities in Den Helder in addition to offices, include a benthic lab, eco-analysis lab, climate rooms, mesocosms and algae culture facilities. Additionally, WMR has an experimental hard substrate garden in the marina on the island of Texel.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are/have the following: 
 you have a master’s degree (or graduation before appointment date) in Biology, Marine Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, or another closely related field;
 you have experience with hands-on laboratory experiments and ecological fieldwork;
 you have demonstrated background or strong interest in ecological modelling and data analysis;
 you have a strong interest in marine ecology and multidisciplinary research;
 you also have strong collaborative skills and are willing to work with a diverse group of scientists, technicians, and project stakeholders with various backgrounds.
Furthermore, you have strong quantitative and preferably technical skills, and the ability to work independently in a challenging environment.
 You also possess: 
you have a proactive, inquisitive, enthusiastic, creative and self-reliant mind-set and you are strongly motivated to obtain a PhD degree.
Finally, you are excellent in written and oral communication skills in English (a minimum of CEFR C2 level language proficiency). For more information about this proficiency level, please visit our special language page .

CONTRACT: 18 months

academictransfer:363942.description:
Wil jij jouw financiële kennis inzetten in een leidinggevende rol binnen een complexe financiële omgeving én zie je scherp waar het slimmer of beter kan? Als teammanager geef je leiding aan de debiteurenadministratie van de Universiteit Utrecht en werk je mee aan digitalisering, procesverbetering en de overgang naar een nieuw ERP-systeem.
 Wat ga je doen? 
Als teammanager geef je leiding aan een team van dertien collega’s en zorg je voor een goede uitvoering van onze debiteurenadministratie. Daarbij combineer je de dagelijkse aansturing met procesverbetering en bereid je je team voor op het nieuwe ERP-systeem dat we binnen de Universiteit Utrecht uitrollen.
 De dagelijkse operatie: je bent verantwoordelijk voor de uitvoering van de dagelijkse werkzaamheden. Je bewaakt de werkvoorraad en de kwaliteit van het geleverde werk en houdt oog voor de dienstverlening binnen de organisatie en daarbuiten;
 Leiderschap: je kent de talenten en drijfveren van de medewerkers en stimuleert hun ontwikkeling en betrokkenheid. Je bevordert de samenwerking binnen het team en zorgt samen met je medewerkers voor goede resultaten.
 Procesmanagement: de afgelopen jaren is fors ingezet op het digitaliseren van de administratie, het verhogen van de efficiëntie en het verbeteren van de (data)kwaliteit. Een proces dat natuurlijk nooit ‘af’ is; als teammanager heb je hierin het voortouw.
 Vervanging ERP: de Universiteit Utrecht staat aan de vooravond van een volledige vervanging van haar huidige SAP-landschap; op 1 januari 2028 wordt een vernieuwd ERP in gebruik genomen. Je werkt mee aan de inrichting en bent de voorbereiding van je team op deze ingrijpende vernieuwing.
Het team Inkomende Geldstroom (IG) is onderdeel van het Administratief Service Centrum (ASC) waarin de administratieve financiële processen van de universiteit zijn gecentraliseerd. Je maakt deel uit van het managementteam van het ASC en rapporteert direct aan de manager van het ASC.
IG verzorgt de centrale debiteurenadministratie voor alle faculteiten en diensten van onze universiteit. Je geeft leiding aan 13 collega’s die samen jaarlijks bijna 65.000 facturen verwerken.
De Universiteit Utrecht heeft een jaarlijkse begroting van € 1,1 miljard. Ruim 150 financials werken dagelijks aan het beheer van deze omvangrijke en complexe geldstroom, van administrateur en treasurer tot projectcontroller en financieel directeur.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je geeft op een betrokken en resultaatgerichte manier leiding en weet medewerkers mee te nemen in veranderingen. Je herkent talenten, stimuleert ontwikkeling en samenwerking en houdt tegelijkertijd oog voor kwaliteit en resultaat. Je houdt overzicht, neemt beslissingen wanneer dat nodig is en kunt omgaan met verschillende belangen en weerstand. Je werkt nauwkeurig en oplossingsgericht en neemt het voortouw bij het verbeteren van processen.
 Een afgeronde hbo-opleiding, bij voorkeur in finance, bedrijfseconomie of bedrijfsadministratie;
 Ruime ervaring in een financiële administratie in een complexe (non-profit) organisatie;
 Ervaring in of interesse in het digitaliseren en optimaliseren van processen en systemen;
 Minimaal 3 jaar leidinggevende ervaring.

We offer a four-year PhD position within the NWO-funded AMASZINC (Analysing and MApping Strontium and Zinc IN Cremations to reconstruct diet, mobility, and funerary practices of ancient human and animal populations) project, which aims to develop new ways of studying mobility, diet, and funerary practices from cremated human and animal remains. The project combines cutting-edge laser ablation techniques with Sr and Zn concentration and isotope ratio analysis to unlock information preserved in burnt bone. The project is carried out in close collaboration with Prof. Christophe Snoeck at Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) and Dr. Klervia Jaouen at Observatoire Midi Pyrénées/CNRS, Toulouse, France, offering opportunities to work across institutions and research fields.
 Your duties 
 investigating mobility and dietary histories as well as funerary practices of Iron Age and Roman populations from the Netherlands, Belgium, Slovenia, and Portugal
 performing laser ablation mapping of cremated bone
 conducting high-precision ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr and δ⁸⁸Sr analyses using TIMS and MC-ICP-MS
 developing and testing new approaches for Zn concentrations and isotope ratio analysis of cremated bone
 presenting findings at national and international scientific conferences
 publishing research findings in international peer-reviewed journals
 completing a paper-based PhD thesis and defending it at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
 participating in the training programme of the SENSE graduate school

REQUIREMENTS:
degree in MSc in Earth Sciences or Archaeological Sciences
 strong scientific motivation and interest in archaeology
 hands-on experience with relevant analytical techniques is an advantage
 affinity with numerical modelling (Python, R)
 readiness to travel and work abroad for short periods of time (especially in Brussels and Toulouse)
 driving license is desirable
 excellent ability to communicate in both written and spoken English
 good social skills

In this position, you will work closely with the Senior Data Steward and Secretary of the Ethics Review Board to support researchers throughout the research lifecycle and contribute to a culture of research integrity, open science, and compliance. In addition, you will also collaborate with other support staff from the VU Library, IT, Legal Affairs and Grants office.
As a Data Steward, you will advise and support researchers, PhD candidates, and research staff on all aspects of research data management, open science, privacy legislation and research ethics compliance. You will help ensure that research data are managed responsibly, securely, and in accordance with national and institutional policies, ethical standards, and applicable legislation.
Working alongside the Senior Data Steward and Secretary of the Ethics Review Committee, you will contribute to the development and implementation of policies, procedures, tools, and support services that facilitate high-quality research within SBE and the VU at large.
You will be part of the SBE Research Office. The Research Office supports the School's research community by providing expertise and services in research funding, project management, ethics, research integrity, data management, open science, research and PhD policy. The office works closely with researchers and faculty leadership to create the conditions for high-quality, impactful, and responsible research.
 Your duties 
 provide advice and guidance to researchers on research data management throughout the research lifecycle
 support researchers in the preparation and review of Data Management Plans (DMPs)
 advise on the secure storage, sharing, publication, and archiving of research data
 promote the application of FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) and open science
 support compliance with privacy legislation, including GDPR, institutional and national policies. This includes support with the preparation of privacy statements, data-processing agreements and data protection impact assessments
 develop and deliver training sessions, lectures, workshops, and guidance materials on research data management and research ethics for researchers, as well as PhD and master students
 collaborate with the Senior Data Steward and University Library staff on implementing and further developing data stewardship services within SBE and the VU
 serve as a point of contact for researchers seeking advice on data-related and ethical aspects of research
 monitor developments in research data management, research ethics, open science, and privacy legislation and translate these into practical recommendations for the faculty
 participate in institutional and national networks on research data management, open science and research ethics

a completed Master's degree, preferably in a relevant field

Are you an experienced international agricultural development professional ready to become a leading advisor in seed systems? 
Do you enjoy working at the intersection of agriculture, innovation, policy, institutions and markets? Would you like to help strengthen seed systems that improve farmers' access to quality seed of improved and locally adapted varieties and contribute to more resilient, equitable and sustainable food systems?
We welcome both established seed-systems experts and senior agricultural-development professionals with complementary expertise in areas such as agricultural innovation, agribusiness, food systems, value chain development, plant breeding, policy or institutional development. You bring either direct seed systems expertise or the ambition and demonstrated potential to develop into a leading seed systems advisor.
We are looking for someone who is open-minded, curious and comfortable working across diverse seed systems and stakeholder groups. You will work primarily in Africa and, where relevant, in Asia and Latin America, building trusted partnerships with farmer organisations, governments, research organisations, NGOs, development partners and a diversity of local, domestic and internationally operating seed companies and entrepreneurs. You will also help connect the strengths of the Dutch seed sector and international development ecosystem to seed sector transformation worldwide.
 Key responsibilities: 
The role combines programme leadership, technical advisory work, acquisition, relationship management and applied research. The balance will vary across programmes and over time, but programme management, technical advisory work and acquisition will form the core of the role.
 Designing, leading and implementing seed sector transformation programmes at national, regional and international levels. These may range from short-term advisory and applied research assignments to large programmes involving substantial budgets, multidisciplinary and transdisciplinary teams, and international consortia.
 Ensuring high-quality programme delivery and effective risk management in collaboration with WSER's legal, financial, procurement and project management teams.
 Acting as a strategic knowledge partner in programmes, including those led by partner organisations, by co-creating knowledge and contributing expertise in evidence generation, programme learning and capacity strengthening.
 Applying systems thinking to analyse seed systems and translate evidence into practical institutional, market and policy innovations that strengthen them and contribute to food system transformation.
 Building long-term, reciprocal partnerships with public, private, research and civil-society actors across seed sectors.
 Facilitating policy dialogue and institutional change, and designing, piloting, scaling and institutionalising innovations across areas such as seed policy and regulation, quality assurance, variety development, seed business development, finance and public-private partnerships.
 Connecting international programmes with the Dutch Diamond approach by fostering collaboration between government, knowledge institutes, the private sector and civil society, and maintaining strategic relationships with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security, Fisheries and Nature, Plantum, SeedNL, Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) and other Dutch partners.
 Leading the acquisition and development of new programmes through concept development, proposal writing, consortium building and donor engagement.
 Strengthening Wageningen Social & Economic Research's international profile through publications and knowledge products, and through participation in conferences and professional networks.
 About the team 
You will join the Food System Transformation team within Wageningen Social & Economic Research, working alongside around ten seed system professionals with diverse international backgrounds, expertise and experience. As an internationally recognised team in seed sector transformation, we combine scientific rigour with a strong commitment to translating knowledge into practice. Together, we support partners worldwide through programme management, strategic knowledge partnerships, applied research and institutional innovation.

REQUIREMENTS:
To strengthen our team, we are looking for someone with:
 A Master's degree in agricultural sciences, plant sciences, economics, social sciences, international development or a related discipline. A PhD is considered an asset.
 At least eight years of relevant professional experience in agricultural development, food systems, seed systems, agribusiness or related fields.
 A systems-thinking mindset and the ability to analyse complex agricultural, institutional, policy and market challenges.
 Expertise in several areas relevant to seed sector transformation, such as agricultural innovation, seed systems, plant breeding, agribusiness, value chain development, institutional development, policy and regulation, market systems development or public-private partnerships. Direct seed-systems experience is an advantage but not essential.
 Proven experience leading complex international programmes involving substantial budgets, multiple partners and multidisciplinary teams.
 Professional experience working across multiple countries in Africa, preferably complemented by experience in Asia and/or Latin America.
 The ability to build trusted partnerships and work effectively with diverse stakeholders, from farmer organisations and governments to research institutes, development partners and domestic and international seed companies.
 A good understanding of, or strong affinity with, the Dutch seed sector and the Dutch ecosystem for international agricultural development, with the ability to connect Dutch knowledge, policy and partnerships to seed sector transformation.
 Excellent analytical, facilitation and communication skills, with an affinity for institutional innovation and organisational change.
 Experience in applied research and in publishing technical reports and/or scientific papers is considered an asset.
 Excellent spoken and written communication skills in both Dutch and English are essential. Dutch is required to engage effectively with government and stakeholders in the Netherlands, while English is the primary working language within the team and in most programmes and partnerships. Proficiency in French is considered an asset. Knowledge of Portuguese and/or Arabic is an additional advantage.
 Willingness to travel internationally.

Wil je als onderzoeker bijdragen aan het behoud van biodiversiteit en de toekomst van onze leefomgeving? Dan is deze kans bij Naturalis in Leiden voor jou! Jij onderzoekt hoe basisscholen de biodiversiteit kunnen versterken en een verrijkende omgeving kunnen worden voor kinderen. Je krijgt volop ruimte om jouw onderzoek naar het vergroenen van basisscholen zichtbaar te maken binnen en buiten de wetenschap. 
 Als postdoc...  
 Krijg je volop kansen om je onderzoek en de resultaten breed uit te dragen. Via publicaties, maar ook op de podia in ons eigen museum of bij de partners in ons netwerk. 
 Word je goed begeleid door ervaren collega’s én krijg je de kans om je eigen ambities waar te maken.
 Doe je waardevolle contacten op. En dankzij onze samenwerking met uiteenlopende partners bouw je aan een stevig profiel als onderzoeker.
 Dit ga je doen 
Jouw onderzoek draagt bij aan een grootschalig overkoepelend NWO-onderzoeksproject gericht op duurzame schoolgebouwen: School Greenovation. Dit project voert Naturalis uit in samenwerking met een breed consortium dat ook bestaat uit de TU Delft, Hogeschool Leiden en de Hogeschool Windesheim. Samen richten we ons op de vraag: hoe kunnen verouderde basisscholen zo gerenoveerd worden dat ze technologisch duurzaam zijn, een gezond leerklimaat bieden voor kinderen én de biodiversiteit in de omgeving versterken? Jouw bijdrage? Jij brengt de (kansen voor) biodiversiteit in kaart en onderzoekt het beeld dat basisschoolkinderen hebben van de flora en fauna om hen heen.
Je werkzaamheden zijn divers: van literatuuronderzoek en data-analyse tot bezoek aan schoolklassen voor dataverzameling en het in kaart brengen van biodiversiteit op de betrokken scholen. Samen met de projectverantwoordelijke geef je vorm aan de verschillende fasen van je postdoc-traject. En met je collega’s en onze partners zorg je dat jouw onderzoek meer wordt dan theorie en impact heeft in de praktijk. Je deelt je bevindingen actief, via wetenschappelijke publicaties, presentaties en door bij te dragen aan co-creatiesessies met de betrokken partners. Ook krijg je de kans om onderwijs te geven, bijvoorbeeld door stage-studenten te begeleiden of een gastles te verzorgen.
 Dit krijg je van ons 
 Een jaarcontract met zicht op verlenging met een jaar na succesvolle evaluatie.
 Een bruto maandsalaris van € 3.768,- tot € 4.897,- bij een fulltime dienstverband (36 uur per week). 
 Eindejaarsuitkering van 3,4% van je bruto jaarsalaris en 8% vakantiegeld.
 Vrije tijd met 27 verlofdagen per jaar bij een fulltime dienstverband. Plús 1 extra dag die je kunt inzetten voor een feestdag die voor jou belangrijk is. 
 Reiskostenvergoeding, afhankelijk van de manier waarop je reist. 
 Pensioenregeling via PFZW, waarbij Naturalis 60% van je premie betaalt.
 Ontwikkelmogelijkheden. We werken samen aan jouw ontwikkeling en begeleiding. Ook heb je onbeperkt toegang tot de opleidingen van GoodHabitz.
 Boeiende kennisevents. Zodat je in je eigen vakgebied én daarbuiten up-to-date blijft. Denk bijvoorbeeld aan onze lezingen en bijeenkomsten over verschillende (wetenschappelijke) onderwerpen. Of haak aan – óf presenteer zelf – tijdens de boeiende interne informatiesessie Naturalis Draait Door.
 Een laptop en een telefoonvergoeding.
 Mooie extra’s als korting op software voor privégebruik, collectieve zorgverzekeringen en fietsplan. Verder krijg je korting in ons museumrestaurant en onbeperkt gratis toegang tot ons prijswinnende museum voor jou en je familie.
 Leuke events zoals elke maand een borrel, jaarlijks een bbq en een spetterend eindejaarsfeest. Liever niet voor jou? Ook helemaal prima natuurlijk. Alle activiteiten zijn vrijblijvend.
 Een unieke werkomgeving in een hypermodern gebouw dat jou – dat kan niet anders! – elke dag trots maakt dat je hier mag werken.
 Daarnaast ligt de wereld aan je voeten 
Letterlijk. Want wat je rol ook is, je draagt elke dag bij aan het behoud van onze planeet. Naturalis Biodiversity Center...

Are you our next PhD candidate in functional data analysis? Are you passionate about developing statistical methodology for complex, dynamic data? Join our team to develop methods for estimating time-varying network structures and detecting structural changes in functional time series.
 Information 
In many scientific fields, observations are increasingly collected in the form of functions rather than simple numerical measurements. Examples include brain signals recorded continuously over time, and economic indicators observed as curves or distributions. Such functional time series often exhibit temporal dependence, non-stationarity, and complex non-Euclidean structures. These features contain valuable information, but they also make conventional statistical methods difficult to apply and can lead to unreliable conclusions.
Network structures provide a useful way to describe the relationships among the components of these complex data. In neuroscience, for example, connections between brain regions may be inferred from functional imaging signals rather than observed directly. Understanding which connections are present, how they evolve over time, and when structural changes occur is essential for scientific interpretation. Existing methods may produce false or missed connections when the observations are dependent, non-stationary, and non-Euclidean.
In this project, you will investigate theoretical tools for analysing dependence structures in functional time series. You will develop new methods and statistical softwares for constructing time-varying networks, detecting structural changes, and controlling false connections in complex settings. The proposed methods will contribute to deeper insights in distinguishing connections and changes from random variation in scientific studies. The PhD candidate will be supervised by Lujia Bai and Jeanine Duistermaat , and will publish in international scientific journals, participate in international conferences, and develop an independent research profile.
You will join the Statistics, Probability and Operations Research (SPOR) cluster in the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science at Eindhoven University of Technology. The cluster offers a collaborative research environment that connects time series analysis, functional data and network analysis. We work closely with external partners who drive innovation and growth, and our research is strongly embedded in applications such as anomaly detection, process monitoring and improvement, weather and climate forecasting, and statistical bioinformatics.
As an ideal candidate, you have a strong affinity for mathematical statistics and rigorous proofs, as well as a passion for developing and implementing novel methods and applying them to real-world data.

REQUIREMENTS:
A master’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Econometrics or related majors.
 Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students.
 Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level).
 Good programming skills preferably in R or Python. Experience in programming with C++.
 Prior knowledge in time series analysis, functional data analysis or functional analysis is of benefit .
 Excellent communication skills.

CONTRACT: 4 years

De Universiteit voor Humanistiek zoekt per 1 december 2026 een Universitair Docent Zorgethiek en Humanistiek (v/m/x) voor 0,6 fte en een tijdelijke aanstelling van één tot maximaal drie jaar.  
 Over de leerstoel: 
Je komt te werken bij de vakgroep Zorgethiek. De vakgroep geniet internationale erkenning vanwege haar interdisciplinaire benadering van zorgethiek en de masteropleiding Zorgethiek en Beleid. Binnen de vakgroep werken we aan de verdere ontwikkeling van zorgethiek als kritisch en interdisciplinair veld van onderzoek en onderwijs, in nauwe verbinding met maatschappelijke praktijken en vraagstukken.
In ons onderzoek en onderwijs benaderen we zorg als een relationele, maatschappelijke en politieke praktijk. Onze expertise bestrijkt een breed terrein, van zorgpraktijken, organisaties en beleid tot zingeving, rouw en verlies, en van disability, inclusie en langdurige zorg tot familie en reproductieve gezondheid, humanitaire zorg, kunst en ecologie. We besteden bijzondere aandacht aan vragen rond afhankelijkheid en relationaliteit, rechtvaardigheid en ongelijkheid, lichamelijkheid en verschil, en de institutionele en maatschappelijke omstandigheden waaronder zorg vorm krijgt. Daarbij verbinden we filosofische en theoretische perspectieven met kwalitatief-empirisch, praktijkgericht en artistiek onderzoek.
 Taken en verantwoordelijkheden: 
Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder meer uit:
 Verzorgen van colleges en werkgroepen binnen de master Zorgethiek en Beleid, waaronder onderwijs op het gebied van zorgethiek en beleid in zorg- en welzijnsorganisaties.
 Verzorgen van colleges, werkgroepen en andere onderwijsvormen binnen de bachelor en, waar nodig, de master Humanistiek.
 Coördineren en, waar nodig, verder ontwikkelen van vakken in samenwerking met collega-docenten.
 Ontwikkelen en beoordelen van toetsen.
 Begeleiden en beoordelen van bachelor- en masterscripties.
 Bijdragen aan curriculumontwikkeling en aan de kwaliteit en organisatie van het onderwijs.
 Participeren in de academische gemeenschap van de vakgroep en de UvH en bijdragen aan een cultuur van zorgzaamheid, betrokkenheid en inclusiviteit.
 Binnen de beschikbare onderzoekstijd de eigen wetenschappelijke expertise onderhouden en waar mogelijk aansluiten bij onderzoeksactiviteiten van de vakgroep.
 We vragen: 
We zoeken een gepromoveerde universitair docent met expertise op het gebied van zorgethiek en een sterk profiel in academisch onderwijs. Je bent gepromoveerd in een voor de zorgethiek relevant vakgebied binnen de geesteswetenschappen, sociale wetenschappen en/of verpleeg-, gezondheids- of medische wetenschappen. Je hebt ruime belangstelling voor de maatschappelijke en institutionele contexten waarin zorg wordt vormgegeven en kunt zorgethische theorie verbinden met vragen rond zorgpraktijken, organisaties en beleid.
Een belangrijk deel van je werkzaamheden ligt binnen de master Zorgethiek en Beleid. Je wordt onder andere ingezet bij het vak Zorgethiek en beleid in zorg- en welzijnsorganisaties. Affiniteit met beleid, beleidsanalyse en/of organisatievraagstukken in zorg en welzijn strekt daarom tot aanbeveling. Omdat deze functie voor 70% uit onderwijs bestaat, zoeken we iemand die zelfstandig verantwoordelijkheid kan dragen voor complexe onderwijstaken, waaronder het verzorgen en coördineren van academisch onderwijs.
Daarnaast ben je breed inzetbaar binnen het onderwijs van de Universiteit voor Humanistiek, in het bijzonder in de bachelor en waar nodig in de master Humanistiek, onder meer voor colleges en werkgroepen, toetsing en scriptiebegeleiding.
Kortom, we zoeken een collega die:

 in staat is studenten te begeleiden bij bachelor- en masterscripties;

 de Nederlandse en Engelse taal op minimaal C1-niveau beheerst, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk;

 affiniteit heeft met de humanistische signatuur van de Universiteit voor Humanistiek.
Daarnaast is het een pre als je kennis van of ervaring hebt met zorg- en welzijnsorganisaties en de institutionele context van zorg. Ook ervaring met beleid of beleidsanalyse strekt tot aanbeveling.
 We bieden:

The candidate will work in an interdisciplinary environment, combining experimental approaches (single molecule fluorescence and biochemistry) with computational methods. The candidate will obtain single-molecule multiplexing data and validate machine learning predictions using the high-throughput data. The successful candidate will collaborate with international partners for therapeutic applications of this research. academictransfer:364014.description:
€3,204 - €4,051; Master's; 38 hours
About the position
 The Southern Ocean plays a disproportionately large role in the global ocean carbon cycle. Its carbon cycling is strongly influenced by zooplankton, especially Antarctic krill and salps, whose fecal pellets drive vertical carbon export. Krill depend closely on sea ice and under‑ice habitats, while salps thrive in warmer, often ice‑free waters. Warming and sea‑ice loss are already shifting their distributions and increasing spatial overlap, with implications for competition, food webs, and fisheries. Yet current ecosystem models represent these key grazers only crudely, leaving major uncertainties in future projections.
 This project asks how changing interactions between Antarctic krill and salps reshape Southern Ocean ecosystems and the global carbon cycle. It will explore how sea‑ice loss, warming, predation and fisheries affect krill and salp population dynamics, and how shifts in their relative dominance alter grazing, fecal pellet production and vertical carbon export. Ultimately, it aims to reduce uncertainty in projections of Southern Ocean functioning under future climate and fishing scenarios.
 What are you going to do?
 You will develop stage‑structured population models for both species, explicitly including life‑history processes, sea‑ice dependence, predation and fisheries. You will couple these models to an ocean-sea‑ice-biogeochemical framework for the Antarctic Peninsula to quantify impacts on vertical carbon export. Finally, you will explore future climate and fishing scenarios to assess how shifts in krill-salp dominance affect Southern Ocean functioning.
 Tasks and responsibilities: 
 Complete and defend a PhD thesis within the official appointment duration of four years
 Develop and analyze stage-structured population models for krill and salp
 Couple the stage-structured models to an ocean-sea ice-biogeochemical framework to quantify how zooplankton life-histories influences vertical carbon export and local carbon cycling
 Publish your results in international scientific journals
 Present your results at meetings and scientific conferences
 Discuss your work in our group meetings, incorporate feedback, and give input to others
 Assist in teaching activities and in supervising bachelor and master students
 Your profile
 Your experience and profile: 
 Completed, or soon-to-be completed MSc in the biological sciences or different fields in the natural sciences (e.g. computational, mathematical, earth or marine sciences) with a strong interest in ecology and modeling
 Demonstrated experience with mathematical modelling, and an ability to learn new concepts and (computational) methods as needed
 A demonstrated ability to work with programming languages such as R, Python, Matlab, or C++
 A keen interest in advancing our understanding of marine ecosystems, polar regions, and/or biogeochemistry
 Proficient communication skills in spoken and written English
 Experience in scientific writing, bifurcation analysis or numerical ocean modeling are considered a plus.
 Our offer
 A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. For this position the University Job Classification profile “Promovendus” (PhD candidate) applies. Your salary will be € 3.204 gross per month in the first year and will increase to € 4.051 in the final year, based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week. In addition, you will receive a 8% holiday allowance and 8.3% year-end allowance.  
 A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants.
 The  Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands  is applicable.
 Besides the salary and a vibrant and challenging environment at Science Park we offer you multiple fringe benefits:
 232 holiday hours per year (based on fulltime) and extra holidays between Christmas and 1 January;
 multiple courses to follow from our Teaching and Learning Centre;
 a complete educational program for PhD students;
 multiple courses on topics such as leadership for academic staff;
 multiple courses on topics such as time management, handling stress and an online learning platform with 100+ different courses;
 7 weeks birth leave (partner leave) with 100% salary;
 partly paid parental leave;
 the possibility to set up a workplace at home;
 a pension at ABP for which UvA pays two third part of the contribution;
 the possibility to follow courses to learn Dutch;
 help with registration at UvA- Housing for a studio or small apartment when you’re moving from abroad. 
 Are you curious to read more about our extensive package of secondary employment benefits, take a look  here .
 About us
 The  Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics  (IBED) is one of eight research institutes of the  Faculty of Science  at the  University of Amsterdam . The research at IBED aims to unravel how ecosystems function in all their complexity, and how they change due to natural processes and human activities. At its core lies an integrated systems approach to study biodiversity, ecosystems and the environment. IBED adopts this systems approach to ecosystems, addressing abiotic (soil and water quality) and biotic factors (ecology and evolution of plants, animals, and microorganisms), and the interplay between those. The IBED vision includes research encompassing experimental and theoretical approaches at a wide variety of temporal and spatial scales, i.e. from molecules and microorganisms to patterns and processes occurring at the global scale. The University of Amsterdam has excellent  high performance computing  facilities. Furthermore, IBED has a dedicated  computational support team  with specialized knowledge of bioinformatics, (geo)database management and scientific programming. IBED also works with non-academic partners to deliver transdisciplinary science for society.
