PhD position: Decision-Making for Heat Transition Planning
Your job
 PhD Position: Decision-Making for Heat Transition Planning under Data Sharing Constraints 
 Can grid operators and other stakeholders make robust decisions when the data they need cannot always be shared? 
 The transition to sustainable heating is one of the biggest challenges of the energy transition. Increasing electrification through technologies such as heat pumps creates new planning and congestion challenges for electricity distribution grids. At the same time, effective planning depends on access to data from multiple stakeholders - including municipalities, distribution system operators (DSOs), and households. However, such data are often fragmented, privacy-sensitive, or unavailable due to technical, legal and organizational constraints.
 As a PhD candidate, you will develop novel decision-making methods that enable robust decisions for heat transition planning despite these data-sharing constraints. Rather than assuming full access to data, your research will investigate how planning and operational decisions can be improved when information is incomplete, uncertain, decentralized or privacy-preserved.
 The project 
 You will join the newly funded  NWO (Dutch Research Council)  KIC project Sharing the Warmth , an interdisciplinary collaboration between Wageningen University, TU Delft, Hogeschool Utrecht, CWI, Dutch municipalities, DSOs, and other societal/industry partners. The project brings together expertise in energy informatics, optimization, data science, social sciences, and governance to develop trusted data-sharing solutions for the heat transition.
 Within the project, you will have the opportunity to collaborate with other PhD candidates and a postdoctoral researcher working on complementary topics including energy data spaces, privacy-preserving data-sharing, governance, and citizen participation. You will also have access to real-world use cases and operational datasets through our network of municipalities, DSOs and industrial partners.
 Your research 
 Your research will investigate how data-sharing constraints shape decision-making for the heat transition in future electricity networks, using flexible electrification technologies with heat pumps as the primary use case. The research will consider not only technical data availability, but also the governance, privacy and stakeholder requirements that determine how data can be shared and used in practice.
 You will explore questions such as:
 What data do municipalities, DSOs, and other stakeholders need for heat transition planning, and how do data ownership and governance arrangements shape the opportunities and barriers for data-sharing?
 How do incomplete, uncertain, or privacy-preserved data influence heat transition planning?
 How can DSOs and municipalities make robust decisions under realistic data-sharing constraints?
 How can flexibility from distributed energy resources be coordinated while respecting data-sharing requirements?
 How can decision-making methods account for varying levels of trust, transparency, and willingness to share data among stakeholders?
 What decision-making methods are most effective when information is decentralized or only partially observable? 
 Depending on the research direction, you may employ techniques from mathematical modelling, machine learning, uncertainty quantification, distributed decision-making, or other data-driven approaches.
 Your duties and responsibilities in this 4-year project include: 
 analysing data requirements, data availability, and socio-technical barriers to data-sharing for heat transition planning;
 investigating how incomplete or constrained data influence planning and operational decision-making;
 modelling the flexibility of heat pumps and other distributed energy resources for congestion management and heat transition planning;
 working together with interdisciplinary researchers to translate stakeholder needs and data-sharing requirements into decision-support methods;
 developing novel decision-making methods for electricity networks with flexible electrification technologies;
 evaluating and validating the proposed methods using realistic datasets and case studies with municipalities and DSOs;
 publishing your research in leading international journals and presenting your work at international conferences.

Your job
 Do you want to shape the future of sustainable wastewater treatment? Do you enjoy working together with stakeholders from the water sector on fundamental research questions? Do you want to better understand nitrous oxide emissions from deammonification technologies to improve their sustainability?  
 Environmental Technology at Wageningen University & Research is looking for a PhD candidate for the research project UNITED. Within UNITED (Understanding and Narrowing Impacts of Targeted N2O Emissions in Deammonification), several stakeholders from the water sector (including technology providers and end users like water authorities and companies) have joined forces with Environmental Technology at Wageningen University & Research to study the mechanisms behind nitrous oxide emissions from deammonification reactors. 
 Nitrous oxide emissions have a large impact on the CO2 footprint of wastewater treatment plants and they prevent the Dutch water authorities to become climate neutral by 2035. The aim of the research project UNITED is to use the increased understanding of nitrous oxide production to come up with mitigation measures. You will study the N2O production data of several full scale deammonification reactors. You will experimentally study the effect of electron donor and acceptor availability to identify strategies for reduction N2O production. Specifically, your duties and responsibilities include
 Conduct bioreactor experiments to obtain fundamental insights in the contribution of different N2O production pathways in deammonification reactors under relevant conditions.
 Analyse N2O production data of several full scale deammonification reactors located at wastewater treatment plants in the Netherlands, as well as (the variation in) composition of the rejection water typically treated in these reactors.
 Develop and test mitigation measures in a full scale deammonification reactor.
 Pro-actively communicate your research findings with partners within and outside of the UNITED consortium.

Contract Manager
Your job
 Are you a Contract Manager who doesn’t wait for movement to happen, but creates movement yourself? Do you gain energy from complex collaborations in which sustainability, business operations, innovation and diverse interests come together? As a Contract Manager at Wageningen University & Research (WUR), you work on strategic facility contracts that contribute to a future-proof, sustainable and circular organization. 
 As a Contract Manager, you will contribute to the further professionalization of contract management within WUR and to achieving sustainable impact through intensive collaboration with suppliers and internal stakeholders. You are responsible for contracts in the areas of Business Travel, Mobility as a Service (MaaS), Cleaning and Furniture . These contracts play an important role in realizing future-proof facility services, sustainable mobility solutions, a pleasant and healthy working environment, and supporting WUR’s circular ambitions.
 Within the Contract Management team, you are responsible for steering performance, collaboration and continuous improvement of strategic contracts. You are not only responsible for contract monitoring, but especially for realizing value: you translate ambitions into concrete agreements, stimulate innovation and ensure that suppliers and internal stakeholders work together to achieve sustainable results.
 Your tasks and responsibilities as Contract Manager: 
 you steer the realization of contract objectives in the areas of quality, cost, service delivery, collaboration and sustainability;
 you translate organizational goals and sustainability ambitions into contract agreements, KPIs, improvement initiatives and concrete results;
 you lead contract reviews, performance meetings and improvement processes with suppliers and internal stakeholders;
 you develop and implement improvements and innovations within contracts in the areas of Business Travel, Mobility as a Service (including the car-sharing project), Cleaning and Furniture;
 you connect internal stakeholders and suppliers and create collaboration focused on continuous improvement, innovation and societal value.
 You work according to the CATS-CM methodology, in which contracts are seen as dynamic steering instruments for collaboration and development. You combine performance management with relationship and impact management and ensure that contracts contribute to WUR’s strategic goals.
 Your team 
 The Procurement & Contract Management department is part of the Facility Services division of Wageningen University & Research (WUR). Our department consists of two teams: Procurement and Contract Management. Both teams are supported by legal advisors and a data analyst.
 The Contract Management team is developing rapidly. WUR is working on further centralization and professionalization of contract management and contract administration. As a Contract Manager, you work together with fellow contract managers, contract owners, internal stakeholders and strategic suppliers to realize added value from contracts.
 In your role, you collaborate closely with disciplines such as Procurement, Facility Management, Finance, Real Estate & Housing, IT, HR, Legal and the business. You also work closely with colleagues responsible for mobility, real estate, facility services and sustainable operations. Together, you ensure that organizational goals and sustainability ambitions are translated into concrete services and measurable results.
 The working atmosphere is professional, open and informal where possible. We take our profession seriously, but value trust, collaboration and helping each other just as much. You are given space to take initiative, propose improvements and truly make an impact.

You move easily between strategy, tactics and operations and know how to connect different interests. You are convincing, organizationally sensitive and able to engage people in sustainable transitions.
 You also bring:

 experience in managing complex contracts and strategic collaborations with external partners;
 experience with stakeholder management and connecting different disciplines within an organization;
 affinity with facility services, mobility, sustainability and achieving societal impact;
 experience with the CATS-CM methodology or willingness to further develop in it.
 You are analytical, proactive and pragmatic. You see opportunities and know how to turn them into concrete improvements. You feel comfortable in an environment with diverse interests and where influence, collaboration and perseverance are needed to achieve results.
 You are someone who does not shy away from tension in collaboration, but uses it as a starting point for improvement. You do not wait for others to move — you initiate movement yourself.

Are you passionate about developing the next generation of statistical methods for an increasingly data-rich world? Do you thrive at the intersection of theory, methodology, and impactful applications? We invite applications for an Associate Professor in Statistics to join our vibrant and internationally recognized research environment at the Mathematical & Statistical Methods group of Wageningen University & Research (also known as Biometris).
Modern science, technology, and society generate data at unprecedented scale and complexity. From genomics and environmental systems to artificial intelligence and digital health, researchers are confronted with high-dimensional data that challenge traditional statistical approaches. To address these challenges, we seek an ambitious scholar with expertise in—or a strong affinity with— Bayesian Statistics , who is eager to contribute to our overarching research programme in high-dimensional statistics .
As Associate Professor, you will play a leading role in advancing innovative statistical methodology for complex, large-scale, and structured data stemming from the Life Sciences. We welcome candidates whose research combines methodological rigor with practical relevance, and who are interested in developing novel approaches for uncertainty quantification, large-scale prediction, model-based learning, causal inference, network learning, or related areas. Experience with Bayesian methods, whether theoretical, computational, or applied, will be considered a strong asset.
You will join a collaborative community of statisticians, data scientists, and domain experts who share a commitment to addressing fundamental scientific questions through cutting-edge quantitative methods. The successful candidate is expected to develop an internationally visible research programme, attract competitive research funding, and build interdisciplinary collaborations across Life Science application domains.
Beyond research, you will contribute to inspiring and innovative teaching in statistics and data science. You will mentor Bachelor’s, Master’s, and PhD students, and help to shape the next generation of quantitative scientists. We value educators who can communicate complex statistical concepts with clarity and enthusiasm, and who are committed to fostering an inclusive and stimulating learning environment.
We are looking for a candidate with a strong publication record, demonstrated scientific leadership, and the ability to connect methodological innovation with real-world challenges. This position offers a unique opportunity to influence the future direction of statistical research within a dynamic academic environment. You will benefit from excellent research infrastructure, access to interdisciplinary collaborations, and a supportive atmosphere that encourages creativity, ambition, and scientific excellence. Moreover, within the Academic Career Framework, you will have the opportunity to grow into a full Personal Professor.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 advancing innovative statistical methodology for complex, large-scale, and structured data stemming from the Life Sciences;
 develop an internationally visible research programme;
 attract competitive research funding;
 build interdisciplinary collaborations across Life Science application domains;
 coordinate and contribute to inspiring and innovative teaching in statistics and data science.
This position is part of the Academic Career Framework (ACF) at Wageningen University & Research. One of the 3 career paths is the Professor Career Path. The aim of this ACF is to achieve a new balance in recognising and valuing academics where both team collaboration and the unique talent of individual scientists are seen, by creating more differentiation in career paths, putting the emphasis on the quality of work and less on quantitative results, doing justice to the individual qualities and ambitions of academics as much as to team performance, promoting all aspects of open science and encouraging high-quality leadership in the academy.
 You will work here 
The research is embedded within the chair group Mathematical & Statistical Methods - Biometris , in particular the Statistics chair, which is led by prof.dr. Carel F.W. Peeters . Your educational development will be co-supervised by ir. Saskia Burgers .
 In this challenging career trajectory: 
 you acquire, lead and implement innovative and creative (inter-)national research projects in Statistics;
 you collaborate with colleagues and supervise PhD students, BSc and MSc theses and you develop and teach courses;
 you contribute to the further development of the Mathematical & Statistical Methods group.

REQUIREMENTS:
We seek an accomplished statistician with a strong track record in methodological research and scientific leadership. The ideal candidate has expertise or a strong affinity with Bayesian statistics and a demonstrated interest in high-dimensional statistical methods. They combine theoretical rigor with an openness to interdisciplinary collaboration and real-world applications. The successful applicant is expected to develop an internationally recognized research programme, attract external funding, publish in leading journals, and contribute enthusiastically to teaching and supervision. Strong communication skills, collegiality, and a commitment to mentoring students and early-career researchers are essential.
 You also possess: 
 A relevant academic background concluded with a PhD in an area relevant to the position (Statistics, Mathematical Statistics, Bayesian Statistics, Biostatistics, or closely related field).
 An inspiring educator with the didactical qualities to provide, develop, and coordinate both undergraduate and graduate Statistic and Data Science education for students from varying backgrounds.
 A strong research profile on the interface between Statistics and Data Science as proven through both foundational and application-oriented publications in reputable international journals as well as a commensurate (inter)national network.
 A strong, future-oriented vision on the role of Statistics in research and education in relation to WUR and the (inter)national Data Science and Artificial Intelligence landscapes.
 The ability and willingness to expand the reach of Statistics within WUR to all science groups and to further integrate educational and research efforts with the chairgroup Applied Mathematics.
This position requires exemplary leadership and communication skills as well as an excellent English language proficiency (a minimum of CEFR C2 level).

Your job
 Do you enjoy working in an innovative, challenging environment with different crops and the latest greenhouse climate technology? Are you proficient in the Dutch language?  As a greenhouse climate specialist, you will be in the greenhouse every day to support colleagues, researchers, and students.  work with automated climate systems (Hoogendoorn, Priva), including setting and monitoring the correct climate in relation to plant growth, weather conditions, and the substrates used;

 are experienced in propagation, cultivation, and harvesting of various crops;

 have technical experience in greenhouses (this is a plus).

 Interested in working in the agriculture of the future? Come and work in the field! Do you enjoy working outdoors, combining technology with plants? wur:16414.description:
Are you interested in working in the Soil Biology Lab and collaborating with 100 pioneering farmers in the Netherlands? Do you have affinity with soil sampling and analyses related to the role of soil biota in supporting a range of soil functions? Within the ReGeNL project, we are looking for a laboratory assistant to provide technical support for the monitoring campaigns of the pioneering farmers participating in ReGeNL. 
There is steadily growing pressure on agriculture and the entire food system to increase global production while promoting sustainability in terms of farmers' incomes, soil health, input use, and environmental and climate impact. Regenerative agriculture is a promising avenue to support a healthy, multi-functional and future-proof soil and farming system. Together with regenerative Dutch farmers, ReGeNL is developing a future-proof agricultural sector in which agriculture goes hand in hand with soil health and nature restoration, and a good revenue model for farmers. Between now and 2030, ReGeNL will start the transition to regenerative agriculture with 1000 farmers. The aim is to make regenerative agriculture the new normal by 2040.
In this role, you will support the monitoring of 100 pioneering regenerative farmers within the ReGeNL program. Wageningen University, together with its partners, is responsible for monitoring and studying changes in the farmers’ management practices and evaluating the outcomes of these changes. Through-out the year, fieldwork will be conducted to monitor various aspects of soil health and to document the management practices applied by these pioneering farmers.
 The successful candidate will be responsible for the following key tasks: 
 Coordinate and lead field sampling campaigns and data collection activities across different soil types and land-use systems in the Netherlands.
 Conduct laboratory analyses to explore the dynamic relationships between management practices, soil biota, and soil chemical and physical properties.
 Collaborate closely with soil biology researchers and technical staff.
 You will work here 
The Soil Biology group integrates knowledge on soil biota across a range of scales from the microbe to the globe. Our mission is “to explore the potential of life to increase the quality of soil”.
Soils are among humankind’s most precious natural resources, but their sustainable use is under serious threat. Our aim is to advance and share knowledge on how soil life can improve the quality and functioning of soils in agroecosystems around the world, and how land management may impact soil life. Our ambition is to cover research across a range of scales and levels of detail to ensure dissemination of fundamental insights: starting with interactions at small-scale hotspots in the soil (in particular the rhizosphere and detritusphere), through management-oriented research at the plot and field scale, towards policy-relevant research at the farm, landscape and regional scale. The soil biology laboratory supports both on-going research of the Soil Biology Group (PhD projects and larger projects) and external analyses. In addition, the lab oversees approximately 25-30 MSc thesis projects per year and contributes to the Soil Biology education programmes at both BSc and MSc levels.

REQUIREMENTS:
You have a background in environmental or agricultural sciences (BSc level) and can easily connect with the realities of Dutch farming.
 A BSc soil biology, soil ecology, environmental sciences, or a related field.
 Affinity with fieldwork and willingness to conduct extensive field sampling campaigns across the Netherlands under varying weather and field conditions.
 Experience working in a laboratory environment using techniques commonly applied in soil science research.
 Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
 A team-oriented attitude.
 Fluency in Dutch, both spoken and written, is required for this role.
 Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team.
 Prior experience in research or academic environments is preferred.
 A valid category B driving license.
Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate their experience with concrete examples from their work both within and outside academia.

CONTRACT: 1 year

wur:16459.description:
Well-designed reward schemes are a crucial step in improving farm-level biodiversity. Do you want to contribute to this, and are you interested in dairy farming systems in the Netherlands? We then have an interesting PhD position for you.
Which reward schemes for biodiversity already exist? Can dairy farmers negotiate about them? Which types of schemes are preferred by dairy farmers, and how do such schemes influence adoption of biodiversity measures at farms? What is the impact on farm income? What are the risks associated with implementing biodiversity measures? Answers to these questions contribute to the design of reward schemes that connect better to the practices of farmers, agribusiness, and financial institutions, and eventually improve biodiversity.
The PhD position is part of the DECISION project (Dairy and Ecology: co-innovating business operations for nature), primarily funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO). The project embraces four fully-funded PhD candidates and a postdoc. It is a transdisciplinary project in which also private companies and other stakeholders actively participate. The focal region is the Alblasserwaard.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Develop a research proposal and a Training and Supervision Plan, to structure the 4-year PhD trajectory.
 Perform the PhD research along four objectives: 
 Analyse reward schemes for biodiversity – considering multiple actors (farms, agribusiness) and types (commercial vs subsidised, local vs national, etc.).
 Evaluate which types of reward schemes are preferred by dairy farmers.
 Assess the impact of reward schemes on farm-level implementation of biodiversity measures, and farm income.
 Analyse risks associated with the implementation of biodiversity measures.
 Disseminate results by publishing papers in scientific journals, presenting in international conferences, and creating content items dedicated to stakeholders.
 Work as a team player, contributing to the activities and wider aims of the DECISION project.
 You will work here 
You will be supervised by Prof. dr. Miranda Meuwissen and dr. Max Koppenberg from the Business Economics (BEC) group ; and Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch from the Animal Production Systems (APS) group of Wageningen University & Research. The work of Prof. dr Miranda Meuwissen focuses on farm economics, risk management and sustainable finance in food and agribusiness. The work of Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch focuses on understanding the complex interactions between livestock, nature (biodiversity and ecosystem services) and economy, to design enabling environments for the transitions to nature-inclusive agroecosystems. Dr. Max Koppenberg works on firm performance and supply chain incentives. The involvement of both BEC and APS illustrates the multidisciplinary nature of the PhD-position.

REQUIREMENTS:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and results-driven candidate who meets the following criteria:
 A successfully completed MSc degree in: 
 Agricultural economics, food and agribusiness, or sustainable finance, with interest in farming systems.
 Animal or crop production systems, with proven interest in farm economics.
 Experience with quantitative methods, such as farm accounting, modelling, or statistical analyses.
 Experience with primary data collection, such as interviews and surveys.
 Excellent writing and presenting skills, for both academic and non-academic environments. For this position, the excellent command of English language (level C1) is a prerequisite. In some cases, an internationally recognised certificate may be required.

CONTRACT: 18 months

wur:16460.description:
Are you a systems thinker passionate about bending the curve of biodiversity loss in agroecosystems? Are you looking for a meaningful research path with impact on the ground? Are you eager to join a stimulating environment, collaborate across academic fields, and engage with private and public actors? Are you enthusiastic to dive into a plurality of views regarding biodiversity and its recovery? Then, we have a PhD position for you. 
Biodiversity recovery is essential to sustain resilient food systems, robust businesses, and healthy societies. A transition to nature-inclusive dairy sector in the Netherlands would be pivotal to biodiversity recovery, because of its influence in shaping landscapes through land use and management, and because of its socio-economic relevance. DECISION is a transdisciplinary project involving farmers, dairy companies, financial and service sectors, and local communities, to co-create and accelerate the transition to a resilient and nature-inclusive future. DECISION will count on a broad group of experts, four fully funded PhDs candidates and one postdoc.
For this position, we are looking for a PhD candidate eager to deal with the understanding of the diverse values of nature (including biodiversity and ecosystem services) across stakeholders, and with anticipating the consequences of adopting nature-inclusive transitions for business and for nature. In that role, you will develop and explore the potential of farm typologies to deal with heterogeneity and tailor a nature-inclusive transition; explore the diverse values of nature among diverse stakeholders; and co-design of scenarios and interventions to support biodiversity and the provision of ecosystem services.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Develop a Research Proposal and a Training and Supervision Plan, to structure the PhD trajectory
 Advancing conceptual thinking by linking farm heterogeneity and typologies, diverse values and valuation of nature, and theory of transitions and transformations
 Conducting and analyzing semi-structured interviews and workshops with stakeholders
 Develop scenario analysis and/or other ‘future’ studies
 Disseminate results by publishing papers in scientific journals, presenting in international conferences, and creating content items dedicated to stakeholders
 Work as a team player, contributing to the activities and wider aims of DECISION project.
 You will work here 
This PhD position will be situated between the Animal Production Systems (APS) group and the Land Use Planning (LUP) group of Wageningen University & Research. APS focuses on unravelling the complexity of livestock systems, and exploring trade-offs and synergies of innovations regarding environmental impact, animal welfare, and economic viability, to design a more sustainable future. The LUP group aims to improve our understanding of landscapes as social-ecological systems and focuses on interventions that relieve the pressure on scarce space, improving the overall landscape quality.
You will be supervised by Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch (APS) and Dr Judith Westerink (LUP). The work of Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch focuses on understanding the complex interactions between livestock, nature (biodiversity and ecosystem services) and economy, to design enabling environments for the transitions to nature-inclusive agroecosystems. The work of Dr Judith Westerink focuses on transformative landscape governance, in particular related to biodiversity and dairy farming systems.

REQUIREMENTS:
You have strong analytical skills, capable of disentangling complex problems and understanding diverse perspectives on the matter. You are a responsible and independent researcher, but also a team player that thrives being part of a larger, collaborative and multi-disciplinary team. You are creative, constructive and open to learn from other disciplines.
 You also have: 
 A successfully completed MSc degree in a relevant field, such as Social Sciences, Environmental Sciences, or Integrative Agricultural/Animal/Plant Sciences
 Acquaintance with mixed-method research, experience with conducting and analyzing interviews, surveys and synthesizing documents
 Affinity with semi-quantitative approaches, scenario analysis and/or shared socioeconomic pathways
 Background with the systems approach and/or interdisciplinary research
 Excellent writing and presenting skills, for both academic and non-academic audiences
For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

CONTRACT: 18 months

wur:16478.description:
Are you interested in the future of Plant Breeding and exploring the genetic potential of plants to develop resilient crops for a sustainable agriculture? Then this vacancy may be of interest to you. 
Crop breeding plays a crucial role in addressing multiple worldwide most pressing challenges, including climate change, biodiversity loss, food and nutrition security, and the long-term competitiveness of agriculture. Yet research efforts, funding opportunities and infrastructure remain fragmented across Europe. What is needed to strengthen crop breeding research and innovation in Europe?
One of the most common targets in crop breeding has been resistance to pests and diseases caused by biotic factors. Recently, crop cultivation is under pressure of combined biotic and abiotic stresses due to the intensification of climate changes. Our research aims to explore plant genetic resources by using advanced biotechnology and molecular breeding tools to create cultivars of crops (with the focus on tomato) that are resistant to different diseases under abiotic stresses.
This postdoc position offers the opportunity to learn the needs for keeping plant breeding innovative in the future, and to apply your research skills in the domain of genetics, plant breeding and phytopathology to create resilient crops.
The postdoc will work with different teams on a few projects including EU projects and other national projects funded by Topsector.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Identifying the needs of future plant breeding
 Designing and conducting research including writing articles
 Supervising MSc and PhD students
 You will work here 
You will work closely with colleagues in multidisciplinary teams of the research group of “Breeding for Resistance” at WUR Plant Breeding. Additionally, you will collaborate with colleagues from other WUR Chair groups including Laboratory of Virology and Laboratory of Phytopathology, and Business Units including Biointeractions.
 Plant Breeding of Wageningen University & Research is a merged unit of Wageningen Research and Wageningen University composed of around 200 people including MSc and PhD students and guest workers. It is a highly international group with more than 30 nationalities, organized in ten research groups. We conduct fundamental, strategic and applied research and provide teaching at all educational (BSc, MSc and PhD) levels. Our research focusses on the genetic basis of traits which are relevant to achieve a sustainable agri- and horticulture. We conduct this research often in partnership with breeding companies, local, regional and state governments.

REQUIREMENTS:
We are looking for a researcher skilled in communication, genetics, plant breeding and/or phytopathology with a collaborative attitude and a keen interest in (resistance) breeding. We prefer candidates with experience in crop genetics and breeding.
The candidates should have most of the following qualifications:
 A PhD degree in a relevant field, e.g. Genetics, Plant Breeding, Plant Pathology/Virology;
 Proven skills in research to unravel molecular genetics of resistance to diseases;
 Excellent planning and communication skills (both oral and written);
 Collaborative personality, interested in working with colleagues and students;
 A proven ability to publish in peer-reviewed journals;
 A good command of English language.
In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level C1 .

CONTRACT: 3 years

Your job
 Would you like to contribute to the further development of innovative analytical methods for food safety? Are you fluent in Dutch? Your initial focus will be on PFAS research, while also contributing to broader contaminant-related projects and the development of new HRMS analytical techniques. 
 Within the Contaminants team, you will be responsible for independently carrying out research and method development, addressing complex analytical chemistry challenges, and improving existing analytical methods.
 Your duties and responsibilities as a Chemical Analyst are: 
 independently carrying out research and method development projects;
 developing, optimizing, and validating LC-MS/MS methods;
 troubleshooting and technically optimizing analytical methods;
 coordinating subprojects and contributing to innovative research activities;
 actively contributing to the further development of PFAS and (GC-)HRMS applications.
 Your team 
 You will join the Contaminants Team at WFSR in Wageningen. The team consists of analytical chemists, researchers, and project leaders who collaborate on innovative analyses and research into chemical contaminants. You will work closely with specialists in PFAS, LC-MS/MS, and (GC-)HRMS and play an important role in further expanding this area of expertise. 
 You will work here  
 At WFSR, we develop innovative solutions for challenges related to food safety, the environment, and public health. The Contaminants team develops and performs high-quality chemical analyses for national and international clients, including the Dutch government, European research programmes, and a wide range of knowledge partners.
 Over the coming years, our PFAS research programme will continue to grow significantly. Alongside ongoing research projects, we are developing new analytical methods, expanding HRMS applications, and exploring innovative techniques for the detection of chemical contaminants. As an Analytical Chemist, you will have plenty of opportunities to contribute to these developments while further advancing your own expertise.
 Your qualities
 You are analytical, independent, and proactive. You enjoy solving complex scientific and technical challenges and thrive in multidisciplinary research teams.
 You also possess:  
 a degree in Analytical Chemistry or a related discipline. The exact education level is less important than having an HBO+/university level of thinking and working;
 experience with LC-MS/MS in an analytical or research environment;
 experience with method development and validation in an ISO/IEC 17025 accredited laboratory (or a comparable quality environment);
 strong communication skills and excellent problem-solving abilities;

 Wageningen Food Safety Research (WFSR) is looking for an ambitious researcher in the field of veterinary medicines.
 Where will you work? 
 At Wageningen Food Safety Research (WFSR), we conduct research into food safety, covering both food for human consumption and animal feed. As a researcher, you will be involved in residue research, among other activities.
 Our residue research focuses, among other things, on detecting pharmacologically active substances, veterinary medicines and growth-promoting substances in food and animal feed. Within these research areas, we conduct monitoring and forensic research and develop new analytical methods to control the use of these substances and detect illegal use. We also develop methods to identify unknown residues and advise national and international authorities on preventing and analysing residues in the food chain.
 You will work in a team responsible for research and for efficiently performing and reporting analyses. Together, you and your colleagues contribute to food safety throughout the food chain and to a healthy living environment.
 Your tasks and responsibilities as a Chemical Researcher will include :
 Act as a researcher within a number of projects, mainly focused on governmental tasks, but also within Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) and EU projects in the field of food safety;

 Build and maintain an international and national scientific network;

 Naturally, you will not be doing this alone. You will work closely with colleagues within the veterinary medicines and growth promoters teams, where three teams work closely together. Because you will be involved in activities across different teams, the work is highly varied.

wur:16485.description:
Are you an experienced economist who wants to help shape future reforms of the EU Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) and support decision-making within the European Commission and Dutch government? As senior researcher quantitative agricultural economics (EU Common Agricultural Policy, CAP) you will lead high-impact analytical research that supports evidence-based policymaking at both Dutch and European levels. 
Using advanced economic modelling and quantitative analysis, you will assess agricultural policy options related to CAP reform, climate and biodiversity targets, farm income support, food security, and agricultural competitiveness. Your analysis will generate insights that contribute to resilient food systems, improved nutrition, more secure farm incomes, and the long-term sustainability of European agriculture.
You will join the International Policy team of Wageningen Social & Economic Research (WSER), part of Wageningen University & Research, one of Europe's leading institutes for applied socioeconomic research in agriculture and food systems. In this role, you will acquire and lead research projects, collaborate with multidisciplinary experts, and engage directly with senior stakeholders in the European Commission and Dutch ministries.
You are a recognised expert in agricultural economics who can translate complex policy challenges into rigorous research programmes, lead multidisciplinary teams, and communicate findings clearly to decision-makers. You bring deep knowledge of the EU Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) and a proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior policy stakeholders. Strong quantitative expertise and familiarity with partial equilibrium modelling (e.g. AGMEMOD) and its use for policy analysis will be essential.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Build trusted relationships with policy stakeholders to gain deep insight into their challenges and analytical needs, driving the acquisition of new research projects.
 Lead the design of complex, multidisciplinary research initiatives , working with clients and research partners to define strategic policy questions, shape analytical strategies, and align organizational research strengths with client needs to generate high-impact findings.
 Lead project teams in delivering high-quality research outputs , applying advanced quantitative methods and bio-economic modelling, including AGMEMOD, to generate policy-relevant insights, while ensuring timely and budget-conscious project delivery.
 Engage with clients on the interpretation of research findings and their strategic and policy implications, supporting evidence-based decision-making and capacity building.
 Contribute to WSER's strategic development strengthening market relevance and business growth while inspiring and supporting junior researchers, building policy-oriented research skills within the International Policy team.
 Your team 
You will join WSER’s International Policy expertise group, a team of 26 highly motivated professionals from a wide range of nationalities working on high-impact policy studies for the Dutch government, the European Commission, and other public international institutions and governments. At WUR, you will be part of a vibrant and diverse international research environment, collaborating with leading experts from around the world. Together, we contribute to solutions for pressing global challenges including food security, climate change, economic sustainability, circularity, biodiversity, nutrition, and health. The team is based across WSER’s offices in The Hague and Wageningen.

REQUIREMENTS:
We are looking for an inspirational researcher with a taste for quality, impact, and team orientation.
 You also possess: 
 An MSc or PhD (preferred) in Economics, Agricultural Economics, or a related field. 
 Extensive experience in applied quantitative bio-economic research and modelling. Familiarity with partial equilibrium models and other advanced analytical approaches. A proven track record of leading multidisciplinary research projects and translating complex evidence into policy-relevant insights.
 Strong knowledge of the EU agricultural sector, the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) , combined with a solid understanding of policymaking processes within the European Commission. Familiarity with the opportunities and challenges facing the Netherlands agricultural sector is a distinct advantage.
 Substantial experience engaging with EU CAP policymakers. A well-developed network within the European agricultural policy landscape and a track record of fund raising are desirable.
 Excellent communication skills , with the ability to inspire colleagues, build lasting partnerships, and communicate effectively in English (C1 level or equivalent). Proficiency in Dutch is a strong advantage.
 You will be based in our office in either Wageningen or The Hague. Working from home is possible to a limited extent.

CONTRACT: 1 year

wur:16544.description:
PhD: Leveraging Adolescent Agency to Improve Food Environments at School
Your job
 Are you a development or behavioural economist interested in how young people make decisions about their health and nutrition? Would you like to conduct experimental research on adolescent nutrition and school food environments in Indonesia? 
 Adolescent nutrition in low- and middle-income countries remains a critical yet understudied determinant of health and development. While policy attention has traditionally focused on early childhood, adolescence constitutes a second window of opportunity for nutritional improvement. It is also a period of substantial emotional, cognitive and social change, in which growing agency and decision-making capacity increasingly shape health behaviours.
 This PhD position is part of a research project examining how adolescent agency can be leveraged in school-based nutrition interventions in Indonesia. The research focuses on food preferences, dietary intake and purchasing behaviour and brings together insights from development economics, behavioural economics and public health nutrition.
 As a PhD candidate, you will be involved in field experiments that explore behavioural mechanisms through which agency may affect food preferences of adolescents. You will conduct extensive fieldwork in Indonesia and work closely with an international and multidisciplinary research team.
 Your duties and responsibilities in this project : 
 conduct co-creation sessions and focus group discussions with local stakeholders;
 contribute to the design and implementation of a behavioural experiments and large-scale randomized controlled trial in secondary schools in Indonesia;
 manage and analyse experimental and survey data using rigorous econometric methods, and prepare pre-analysis plans, research reports and academic papers;
 communicate and collaborate local research partners and stakeholders, and contribute to dissemination meetings, policy briefs and academic conferences.
 You will work here

 The project brings together researchers from Wageningen University & Research, Erasmus University Rotterdam and Universitas Sebelas Maret. You will collaborate closely with researchers across these institutions throughout the project.
 The empirical research will take place in and around Solo, Central Java. You will therefore spend a considerable amount of time in Indonesia, where you will be hosted by the Faculty of Economics and Business at Universitas Sebelas Maret during fieldwork. You will also spend time at Erasmus University Rotterdam to engage with the wider research team.
 Your qualities
 You are an enthusiastic and motivated researcher with a strong interest in applied research in development and behavioural economics. You enjoy combining rigorous quantitative research with extensive fieldwork and engagement with research participants and stakeholders. You are able to collaborate effectively within an international and multidisciplinary research team, and have strong organisational and communication skills.
 You also possess:  
 a master’s degree in economics, development economics, behavioural economics, health economics, or related fields; 
 strong econometric skills, preferably including experience with experimental or impact-evaluation methods;
 first experience with original data collection, field research, or behavioural experiments, preferably in a low- or middle-income country;

wur:16553.description:
Are you a systems thinker passionate about bending the curve of biodiversity loss in agricultural landscapes? Are you looking for a meaningful research path with impact on the ground? Are you eager to join a stimulating environment, collaborate across academic fields, and engage with private and public actors? Are you enthusiastic to dive into effective planning and governance arrangements for biodiversity recovery in agricultural landscapes? Do you speak English and Dutch? Then, this PhD position might be the perfect fit for you. 
Biodiversity recovery is essential to sustain resilient food systems, robust businesses, and healthy societies. A transition to a nature-inclusive dairy sector in the Netherlands is pivotal to biodiversity recovery, because of its influence in shaping landscapes through land use and management, and because of its socio-economic relevance. DECISION is a transdisciplinary project involving farmers, dairy companies, financial and service sectors, and local communities, to co-create and accelerate the transition to a resilient and nature-inclusive future. DECISION will count on a broad group of experts, four fully funded PhDs candidates and one postdoc.
For this position, we are looking for a PhD candidate eager to deal with the complexity of public and private governance efforts coming together in landscapes and at farm level, and the need to design coordinated action. In that role, you will build on and integrate the work of your fellow PhD candidates, co-develop a theory of change integrating coordinated public and private action and monitoring, explore synergies and tensions in multi-actor governance and planning, and help bridge research and education.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Develop a Research Proposal and a Training and Supervision Plan, to structure the 5-year project with a 0.8fte PhD trajectory
 Advancing conceptual thinking by linking and comparing business-to-business approaches with collective action and landscape governance
 Conducting and analyzing semi-structured interviews and workshops with stakeholders
 Implement a Theory of Change approach and other approaches for knowledge co-production with stakeholders
 Disseminate results by publishing papers in scientific journals, presenting in international conferences, and creating content items dedicated to stakeholders and students
 Work as a team player, contributing to the activities and wider aims of DECISION project.
 You will work here 
This PhD position will be situated between the Land Use Planning Group of Wageningen University & Research and the Animal Production Systems (APS) group . The LUP group aims to improve our understanding of landscapes as social-ecological systems and focuses on interventions that relieve the pressure on scarce space, improving the overall landscape quality. APS focuses on unravelling the complexity of livestock systems and exploring trade-offs and synergies of innovations regarding environmental impact, animal welfare, and economic viability to design a more sustainable future.
You will be supervised by Dr Judith Westerink (LUP) and Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch (APS). The work of Dr Judith Westerink focuses on transformative landscape governance, in particular related to biodiversity and dairy farming systems. The work of Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch focuses on understanding the complex interactions between livestock, nature (biodiversity and ecosystem services) and economy, to design enabling environments for the transitions to nature-inclusive agroecosystems.

REQUIREMENTS:
You have strong analytical skills, capable of disentangling complex problems and understanding diverse perspectives on the matter. You are a responsible and independent researcher, but also a team player that thrives being part of a larger, collaborative and multi-disciplinary team. You are creative, constructive and open to learn from other disciplines.
 You also have: 
 A successfully completed MSc degree in a relevant social science, such as Spatial Planning, Public Administration and Governance, Institutional Economics, Political Science or (Rural) Sociology
 Demonstrated affinity with biodiversity or other environmental topics
 Acquaintance with mixed-method research, experience with conducting and analyzing interviews, surveys and synthesizing documents
 Affinity with inter- and transdisciplinary approaches, and designing interactive sessions with stakeholders
 Excellent writing and presenting skills in English as well as Dutch, for both academic and non-academic audiences
For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

CONTRACT: 5 years

Your job
 As a senior researcher, would you like to lead innovative research focused on understanding and reducing emissions from the poultry sector? At Wageningen Livestock Research, you will have the opportunity to play a key role as a scientific project leader in developing new knowledge and solutions to issues relating to greenhouse gases, nitrogen, particulate matter, bioaerosols and odour.
 Within the Emissions & Manure Valorisation department, you will take the lead on research projects and work on the acquisition, development and implementation of research proposals.  Using your expertise in the field of poultry (particularly laying hens, broilers and broiler breeders), you will lead multidisciplinary project teams and provide substantive direction for research into house ventilation and air quality, the formation and emission processes of substances, measurement methods and emission-reduction measures. You will combine scientific depth with project leadership and contribute to knowledge that is directly applicable in policy and practice.

 developing research proposals and programmes;

PhD: Modelling Impacts of Agricultural Practices on Soil Ecosystem Services
Your job
 The Earth Systems and Global Change Group at Wageningen University and Research invites applications for a PhD position (4 years) in a challenging project titled: “Modelling impacts of agricultural practices on soil ecosystem services across Europe”.
 Preserving and restoring agricultural sustainability in Europe requires a monitoring framework quantifying how single and combined agricultural management practices affect European soil ecosystem services. The project aims to develop site specific recommendations for the implementation of agricultural practices in arable farming systems that enhance their contribution to a sustainable environment. The project is part of an ongoing European research project with 17 research partners. By finetuning and extending existing regional soil health assessment frameworks to assess the integrative contribution of crop, soil, nutrient and water management practices, this project will deliver new knowledge to enable farmers and policy makers to improve the ecosystem services the soil supplies, and to enable decision-makers to explore scenario outcomes, assess impacts and incorporate the results into soil quality related policy recommendations at national and EU level.
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 As a PhD researcher, you will expand and improve an existing modelling framework to assess carbon and nutrient flows, and soil functions contributing to multiple ecosystem services, and the impact of management measures on regional level, assembling empirical and process-based algorithms considering agronomic and environmental impacts. You contribute to the following activities:

wur:16592.description:
How to best incorporate New Genomic Techniques to solve challenging issues in plant breeding? The recent approval by the European Parliament of new legislation to allow application of gene editing approaches in plant breeding, offers new opportunities to address this. One such challenge is to improve complex traits such as crop tolerance to dynamic environmental conditions in the current era of global climate change and how to best incorporate this in plant breeding strategies.
Anticipating the new legislation, the INPROBED project has been granted, which aims to precisely identify and modify cis -regulatory elements and transcription factor genes that control key physiological pathways to specifically adjust targeted gene expression to reshape complex traits.
The project will develop a breakthrough science-enabled technology platform to improve tomato heat, drought and nutrient deficiency tolerance and the nutritional status of tomato fruits for human health. In this project, you will investigate the tomato response to Zn and Fe deficiency and design strategies to improve the Zn/Fe nutritional status of tomatoes for human health.
You will generate dedicated (single-cell) transcriptional data sets feeding into the MNase-defined cistrome occupancy (MOA-seq) analysis of transcription factor binding of tomato promoter elements controlling the Zn and Fe deficiency responsive gene expression. You will design specific constructs to edit transcription factor genes and their target promoters, and analyse the effects of optimized gene expression regulation on plant performance under optimal and field-like conditions at the Netherlands Plant Eco-phenotyping Centre. Your research aims to improve tomato Zn and Fe uptake under regular field conditions and to enhance the Zn and Fe nutritional status of tomato fruits.
INPROBED is part of the prestigious European Innovation Council (EIC) Pathfinder Challenge programme addressing innovative biotechnology for climate resilient crops. It brings together excellent expertise from world-leading European research institutions and companies. You will work closely together with researchers across the consortium to predict and edit targeted gene promoters, to design relevant constructs for gene editing and to evaluate the gene-edited plants to establish this topic firmly into the plant breeding domain.
Within Wageningen University, you will be embedded in the Laboratory of Genetics of the Plant Sciences Group, and collaborate with researchers and thesis students investigating the genetic basis of plant adaptation to the environment, focusing on plant nutrition, metal tolerance and photosynthesis. Your research is expected to deliver fundamental insights into the genetic regulation of tomato gene expression and provide strong experimental validation of the technology platform to improve complex crop traits through gene editing of gene expression regulators.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 To design the experimental setup for gene expression analysis of tomato response to Zn and Fe deficiency, and of Zn and Fe loading into the developing fruit.
 The biological interpretation of MOA-seq analysis with respect to the tomato response to Zn and Fe deficiency.
 The experimental validation of gene-edited tomato plants with respect to plant growth and development and their ionome under optimal, natural and mineral-stress conditions.
 To establish a fruitful collaboration with international partners in the project and to supervise a part-time technician on the project.
 To write manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals reporting on the results of your research.
 Your team 
You will work with international partners in the project and with other members in the Botanical Genetics team of the Laboratory of Genetics of Wageningen University, which is led by Prof. Mark Aarts You will work in close collaboration with a technician to be appointed on the project.
 You will work here 
Wageningen UR has a global reputation for its ground-breaking research and innovative education in the fields of food and health, sustainable agrosystems, the rural environment, and societal development - all of which make an essential contribution to the quality of life, i.e. the supply of safe and healthy food and drink, on the one hand, and the chance to live, work and play in a balanced ecosystem with a large variety of plants and animals on the other. Within Wageningen UR, the Plant Sciences Group brings together science education and scientific, strategic and applied research in the fields of biology, of plants in relation to their environment, of plant-related organisms and of plant production. The Laboratory of Genetics is interested in heredity in general, in particular the origin, architecture and consequences of genetic variation of a wide range of organisms across the biological kingdoms.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are an ambitious, curiosity-driven and collaboration-oriented plant scientist, with:
 a strong academic track record and a PhD in plant biotechnology, plant molecular genetics or a related topic;
 experience with plant mineral homeostasis and/or tomato research;
 demonstrated expertise in the analysis of large data-sets;
 a strong interest in experimental research;
 an excellent oral and written English communication skills.
In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level C1 .

CONTRACT: 30 months

wur:16615.description:
PhD position on local food web dynamics within offshore wind farms in the North Sea POWER (Progress in Offshore Wind Ecological Research) consortium. 
As offshore wind farms rapidly expand in the North Sea, mitigating their ecological impact on marine ecosystems is critical. The North Sea POWER project addresses this challenge by filling vital knowledge gaps regarding underwater noise, biomass and water flows, and wildlife disturbance (such as seabirds and bats) to support a sustainable green energy transition. By reducing uncertainty in models and identifying effective mitigation options, North Sea POWER supports offshore wind development that protects marine ecosystems while contributing to a sustainable energy future.
The project is funded through the Dutch Research Agenda (NWA), developed in collaboration with the Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy.
Led by Wageningen University & Research, the project brings together a transdisciplinary consortium of leading academic institutions, societal stakeholders, conservation organisations, and energy sector partners. More about the consortium .
This position is one of twelve PhD and postdoc positions across the consortium. You will be part of a team working on shared questions, with joint meetings, fieldwork and training alongside your own project. You will be hosted at Wageningen Marine Research in Den Helder, where you will study how fouling communities in offshore wind farms affect local food web dynamics and carbon cycling in close collaboration with Wageningen University. Part of the molecular lab work will be performed in the lab of Marine Animal Ecology in Wageningen.
 Are you interested in how biofouling communities in offshore wind farms affect local food web dynamics and carbon cycling? 
We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to join our research team on biofouling with a focus on quantifying how biofouling communities influence primary and secondary production and blue carbon sequestration in the seabed. By combining laboratory experiments, in-situ fieldwork observations, and ecosystem modelling, your work will help refine current ecosystem-scale models and inform environmental impact assessments.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 conduct laboratory experiments to measure and quantify grazing rates, carbon biomass, prey preferences, particle export, and faeces sinking velocity rates across different fouling species;
 execute field surveys from research vessels;
 integrate empirical data into conceptual models;
 publish research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present them at national and international conferences;
 mentor BSc/MSc students.
 Your team 
You will be part of Wageningen Marine Research (WMR – Den Helder), as a member of the Theme Team North Sea Reefs with Dr. Joop Coolen , and Dr. Ninon Mavraki as your daily supervisors, and you are also part of the Marine Animal Ecology Group (MAE) supervised by the Associate Professor Reindert Nijland at Wageningen University and Research. In Den Helder a broad group of scientists, analysts, field workers and students work on a variety of topics, such as benthic ecology, seals, seabirds, bats and other species. You will be a member of the theme team North Sea Reefs, with multiple colleagues specialising in the ecology of natural and artificial reefs in the North Sea. Furthermore, you will have the opportunity to design experiments involving molecular tools, such as eDNA and DNA metabarcoding, which then will be performed at the molecular laboratory of MAE in Wageningen University.
 You will work here 
The position is available within Wageningen University & Research at the Marine Animal Ecology group. The organisation has good and flexible employment conditions, including good education and training facilities for PhD students. Your working location will be at Wageningen Marine Research in Den Helder, the Netherlands, where the daily supervisors Joop Coolen and Ninon Mavraki are located. WMR is an applied research institute with 3 locations (Den Helder, IJmuiden and Yerseke) in the Netherlands. Research areas in Den Helder include coastal and offshore North Sea, tropics and (ant)arctic regions. In addition to ecological research, WMR advises the government regarding protection of species and habitats, pollution, and other anthropogenic interactions with ecology, and collaborate with industry, i.a. to study nature inclusive designs. Facilities in Den Helder in addition to offices, include a benthic lab, eco-analysis lab, climate rooms, mesocosms and algae culture facilities. Additionally, WMR has an experimental hard substrate garden in the marina on the island of Texel.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are/have the following: 
 you have a master’s degree (or graduation before appointment date) in Biology, Marine Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, or another closely related field;
 you have experience with hands-on laboratory experiments and ecological fieldwork;
 you have demonstrated background or strong interest in ecological modelling and data analysis;
 you have a strong interest in marine ecology and multidisciplinary research;
 you also have strong collaborative skills and are willing to work with a diverse group of scientists, technicians, and project stakeholders with various backgrounds.
Furthermore, you have strong quantitative and preferably technical skills, and the ability to work independently in a challenging environment.
 You also possess: 
you have a proactive, inquisitive, enthusiastic, creative and self-reliant mind-set and you are strongly motivated to obtain a PhD degree.
Finally, you are excellent in written and oral communication skills in English (a minimum of CEFR C2 level language proficiency). For more information about this proficiency level, please visit our special language page .

CONTRACT: 18 months

Machine Learning/AI Researcher and Project Leader
Your job
 Are you an experienced machine learning and data science professional who wants to make a real-world impact? Do you have a specialisation in machine learning and affinity with project management? Do you want to apply advanced AI solutions to contribute to a more sustainable and better world? We,  Wageningen Food & Biobased Research (WFBR), are looking for a researcher data & modelling.  Are you the one who will strengthen our team? 
 What will you do? 
 As a machine learning researcher, you will initiate and work on innovative data-driven solutions in the bioeconomy and food domains. One example is improving fermentation screening for plant‑based ingredients, a process that is traditionally slow because each substrate–strain combination behaves differently. By applying machine learning to historical experimental data, we can predict high‑potential combinations that support the creation of innovative and sustainable food products. Another example is using large language model (LLM) tools to automatically extract and structure fragmented information from internal and external sources for use in our digital solutions.
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 initiation of new projects / ideas for acquisition by shaping new applied research propositions and supplying the insights needed to convey the value of AI solutions to partners & clients;
 leading projects in which you and your team design and develop new AI solutions. Off course translating research questions into robust machine learning implementations, including preprocessing, model training, validation and deployment is part of your role;
 collaborating enthusiastically with domain specialists and software developers to integrate data‑driven models with mechanistic or physics‑based models and domain expertise;
 showing thought leadership on applying data & AI-solutions in the food & biobased domain: where are the big leaps, how can we actively bring the benefits of data & AI to our customers in this domain?
 Your team 
 You will work as an expert within the expertise group  Wageningen Food & Biobased Research . Together with the adjoining expertise Computer Vision it comprises about 16 diverse specialists ranging from software development to AI/ML research. At DSI, our mission is to unlock the full potential of data and AI to help transform food and biobased systems into sustainable, resilient and innovative sectors — through science, collaboration and real‑world application.
 Our projects require close interaction with WFBR domain specialists, with whom you will play a key role in translating state‑of‑the‑art digital techniques into models that meet their scientific and operational needs. 
 You will work here  
 WFBR operates at the intersection of science, industry and government, delivering applied research and innovation projects funded by both public and private partners. You will be part of a multidisciplinary environment within WFBR, working closely with experts in food technology, microbiology and chemistry. Knowledge sharing is central to how we work: we meet several times a week in Wageningen to exchange ideas, review project progress, and continuously improve our approaches. You will collaborate with business developers, researchers, software developers and clients. You will contribute to impactful applied research in the domains of food and biobased materials.
 Your qualities
 You have solid experience with AI‑ and machine‑learning‑based approaches and easily connect with colleagues from other areas of expertise, enjoying the dynamics of multidisciplinary teamwork. You are comfortable explaining complex technical concepts to non‑technical stakeholders/colleagues and can translate digital approaches into practical, usable solutions. You are proactive, innovative and a strong team player who contributes positively to collaboration and project success.
 You also possess:  
 a PhD in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Science or a related field;
 at least 3 years of hands‑on experience in AI / machine learning development (excluding PhD);
 proven expertise in machine learning and generative AI methodologies (in the range of: LLMs, RAG systems, agentic AI, feature engineering, model selection and validation, supervised and unsupervised learning, optimization techniques, (deep) neural networks, probabilistic methods and statistics, data visualization, natural language processing);
 experience or strong affinity with incorporating domain knowledge and constraints into data-driven models (Hybrid Modelling). Knowledge & experience in food and biobased domains is a plus;
 proficiency in Python and modern machine‑learning development, including version control (Git), testing, and reproducibility; experience with cloud-based solutions (e.g., Azure) is a plus.
 In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position, a C1  level of proficiency  in English is required.
 We offer
 Wageningen University & Research offers excellent  terms of employment . A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include:
 working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
 sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
 there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
 a fixed year-end bonus of 8,3%;
 excellent pension scheme.
 In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. We offer, depending on your experience, a competitive gross salary of between €4220,- and €6471,- for a full-time working week of 36 hours, in accordance with the CLA Wageningen Research (scale 11). Additionally, For this role a contract for 30 hours a week can be discussed. As for your contract, we initially offer a one-year contract that can be extended - if possible within (company) organizational circumstances - on good performance. Of course, we are happy to have a conversation with you if you have any questions about this.
 Wageningen University & Research offers plenty of opportunities for growth and development, with a strong internal recruitment policy and excellent training programmes.
 You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment. 
 Coming from abroad
 Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees. 
 Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. If you come with a partner, we offer a Dual Career group program organized by our  Welcome Center . This program helps your partner to get familiar with the Dutch culture, labour market and assists your partner to find a job.
 Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's  International Community page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.
 Important information
 For more information about the position, please contact Henk Wensink, Research Manager, via e-mail: henk.wensink@wur.nl  or by phone: +31 317 48 55 86.
